    ../ChrononTemplate/docs/REFERENCE_ARTICLE_STYLES.md:6:- **Title cards:** Each article transitions to a black frame with its related YouTube title centered in white. The NBA title uses bold italic sans serif; the synthetic-weed title uses a restrained serif treatment.

    ../ChrononTemplate/docs/REFERENCE_ARTICLE_STYLES.md:8:- **Motion and timing:** Two 8-second, 30 fps clips. The article holds for about 3.5 seconds, then crossfades to the centered title over 0.4 seconds and holds to the end.
    ../ChrononTemplate/docs/REFERENCE_ARTICLE_STYLES.md:9:- **Layers and source:** The article and title are separate SVG-authored raster assets, used as separate Chronon image layers. `build_reference_article_previews.mjs` regenerates the assets and native render plans.

    ## Pack layout (by animation category)
    
    The pack sources are grouped by the kind of animation they author. Headers and
    sources mirror each other under `include/chronontemplate/` and
    `src/chronontemplate/`, so a pack is found by category first, family second.
    The retired map-beat API was replaced by `ModernMapPack`; callers should use
    `ModernMapSpec` and `composeModernMap()` for styled labels and authored camera
    moves. `MapTextRole` exposes title, primary/secondary location, data-value,
    legend, and attribution typography presets. `ModernMapSpec` can add independently
    revealed subtitle/attribution, data cards, legend rows, and multi-segment callout
    leaders. Geographic projection and provider attribution metadata remain owned
    by RenderingGen; ChrononTemplate accepts already-positioned editorial elements
    and does not implement geographic projection.
    
    ### Tactical territory fill
    
    `include/chronontemplate/map/TacticalFillPack.hpp` exposes
    `addTacticalFill()`, the native shape-only version of the
    `territory_tactical_fill` look: a near-black plate, minor/major grid, the green
    territory, a broad red glow, a tighter orange glow, a crisp white outline, and
    a late title/subtitle. Each input ring is a closed polygon already projected to
    canvas coordinates; the pack does not read GeoJSON, reproject coordinates or
    run OpenCV. Rings may be passed as GeoJSON-style closed loops (the duplicate
    last point is dropped).
    
    ```cpp
    TacticalFillSpec spec;
    spec.regions = {{{520.f, 360.f}, {860.f, 300.f}, {980.f, 520.f},
                     {760.f, 700.f}, {480.f, 560.f}}};
    spec.title = "JERUSALEM";
    spec.subtitle = "Capital of Israel";
    const TacticalFillComposition fill = addTacticalFill(scene, spec);
    ```
    
    The territory grows from its centroid over `revealFraction` of the clip. That
    is a native transform reveal, not the reference's circular raster mask; the
    red/orange halos are Chronon3d shape glows, not a Gaussian-blur compositing
    pass. The title starts at 42% and is fully in by 62%, matching the editorial
    beat of the reference. `TacticalFillSpec` exposes the palette, grid spacing,
    outline/glow widths, text typography and text positions; attribution and geo
    provenance stay with the caller/RenderingGen. The sample contract
    (`chronontemplate.tactical-fill-sample.v1`) accepts optional `canvas`, `title`
    and `subtitle` fields, and `chronontemplate_emit_tactical_fill` uses them, so a
    caller such as RenderingGen's `map-tactical-fill` supplies the place name and
    canvas without rebuilding the emitter.
    
    ```text
    important_phrases/          phrasing and titling, one subdir per family
      ImportantPhrasePack            shared look + plan data types
      typewriter/                    fifteen typed animations, `_` cursor
      apple/                         modern restrained phrase presets
      highlight/                     long phrases with animated under-phrase accents
      didone/                        editorial Didone title pack
    short_phrases/              ShortPhrasePack — 26 surviving recipes for phrases of 1–5 words
                                (+ short_phrase.decor.star_bumper, semantic emphasis, exit modes)
    single_images/              ImageAnimationPack — one-image 2.5D entrances
    multiple_images/            MultiImagePack — duo/trio/quad/penta boards, story reels with captions
    backgrounds/                BackgroundPack — editorial documentary/grid/scan/dust looks from shape layers
    entities_with_text/         DocumentarySnapshotPack + YouTubeSubscribe
    map/                        ModernMapPack + MapFxPack + TacticalFillPack — styled plates,
                                map FX and the native tactical territory fill
    camera_roll/                TitleCameraPack + SceneCameraPack — camera-only motion
    transitions/                TransitionPack — eight rapid light looks
    captions_dataviz/           CaptionsDataVizPack — PCM beat grid, beat-timed captions, bar + step-line charts
    composers/                  LayoutComposer — flex row/column/grid boards plus FLIP moves
    fast_intro/                 FastIntroPack — independent short opening composition
    date_timeline/              DateTimelinePack — classic date rail and chronology
    ```
    
    hand-maintained:
    
    ```shell
    cmake --build build/dev --target chronontemplate_emit_short_phrase_catalog
    ./build/dev/chronontemplate_emit_short_phrase_catalog > catalog/short_phrase_motion.v1.json
    ```
    
    The emitter is fail-closed (a malformed pack aborts the emit instead of shipping
    a catalog the consumer would reject), and
    `tools/short_phrases/test_short_phrase_catalog.py` (CTest:
    `chronontemplate_short_phrase_catalog_contract`) pins the document and fails when
    the committed file drifts from what the C++ pack emits today.
    
    ### React text-effect adaptations
    
    Two supplied React components have deterministic native short-phrase recipes:
    `short_phrase_product_split_flap_text` and `short_phrase_product_scroll_reveal`.
    Their `adaptation_note` appears in the catalog and generated manifest. Live
    randomized split-flap tiles and viewport-driven ScrollReveal scrubbing are not
    capabilities of these offline RenderPlans. The C++ pack uses native glyph/word transforms and frame-based
    reveals; it does not claim those browser-only interactions are preserved.
    
    Build the emitters, regenerate the canonical catalog and emit only the two
    surviving React-derived V3 plans (1920×1080, 30 fps, 210 frames):
    
    ```shell
    cmake --build build/dev --target chronontemplate_emit_short_phrase_catalog chronontemplate_emit_short_phrase_plans
    build/dev/chronontemplate_emit_short_phrase_catalog > catalog/short_phrase_motion.v1.json
    build/dev/chronontemplate_emit_short_phrase_plans out/short_phrase_react_text_v1 --react-text-only
    
    CLI=../Chronon3d/build/chronon/linux-video-fast-dev/apps/chronon3d_cli/chronon3d_cli
      --cli ../Chronon3d/build/chronon/linux-video-fast-dev/apps/chronon3d_cli/chronon3d_cli
    python3 tools/important_phrases/build_kinetic_type_editorial_v1.py \
      --out build/kinetic_type_editorial_v1 --render --scene canary_text_word_pop_focus \
      --cli ../Chronon3d/build/chronon/linux-video-fast-dev/apps/chronon3d_cli/chronon3d_cli
    ```
    
    Use `--render-all` for the complete 24-plan canary set. Vulkan exports start in
    sequential bounded-frame renderer processes; a failed range is bisected until
    it passes. Raw frame ranges are joined and encoded once with NVENC at constant
    30 fps. Use `--render-from <plan>`
    to resume a stopped batch after the last verified plan. The
    pack's contract verifies stable ids, finite bounded
    parameters, keyframe/lifetime integrity, UTF-8 semantic spans, safe-area bounds,
    scene handoff overlap, palette/type/background coverage and renderer-native
    plan schemas. A renderer validation or canary establishes contract support,
    not pixel equivalence to an unprovided reference-video frame.
    
    ## Documentary and archival web stills
    
    `include/chronontemplate/web/DocumentaryReferenceStills.hpp` exposes four distinct
    static 1920×1080 native C++ recreations of the supplied video screenshots through
    `chronontemplate::web::buildDocumentaryReferenceStillPlans()`: a highlighted tax-status
    excerpt, an 80s CRT headline, a 1972 newspaper-style rainmaking headline, and a warm
    Pinto documentary text frame. The plans are render-plan V3 data and are emitted by:
    
    ```shell
    cmake --build build/release-fast --target chronontemplate_emit_web_documentary_reference_stills
    ./build/release-fast/chronontemplate_emit_web_documentary_reference_stills out/web_documentary_reference_stills_v1/plans
    tools/web_presets/render_web_documentary_reference_stills.sh
    ```
    
    The render script writes one PNG per composition; it creates no video.
    
    ## Boundary
    
    This module owns recipes. The motion core owns space/time evaluation, and
    Chronon3d owns rasterization, content bytes and font layout. A file belongs here
    when it is a composition recipe over `MotionScene`; a file belongs in the core
    when it is the primitive the recipe is written with.
    
    Two rules keep the move out of Chronon3d possible without breaking its SDK:
    
    - installed header paths and public signatures stay frozen — a recipe may move
      behind a registry, but `chronon3d::presets::MotionParameters` (referenced by
      `LayerBuilder::motion()`) cannot move out of the engine's public surface;
    - the dependency points one way: this module consumes the core and the engine,
      the engine does not link this module;
    - the module owns no font, no glyph, no raster and no matrix maths: text shaping
      and content bytes are `ContentHost`'s answer, the matrix is the motion core's.
    
    ## Canonical ownership
    
    ```text
    RenderingGen owns editorial intent.
    ChrononTemplate owns composition.
    ChrononMotion owns space and time.
    Chronon3D owns content and pixels.
    ```
    
    `scene.text()` is an orchestration facade only: it delegates to
    `ContentHost::createText()`. It is not a font, shaping, glyph or raster API.
    The `ContentHandle` returned by Chronon carries an opaque identity, measured
    metrics and a fingerprint. Motion3D never interprets the text or recomputes its
    layout. Stable element/cluster animation is a Chronon3D capability; the current
    ADR-032 layer record carries the complete content identity, while a future
    additive element-state record must be implemented by Chronon3D before Template
    can expose per-cluster motion.
    
    ## Chronon ABI handoff
    
    `FrameSubmission` now exposes the final `projection × view × world` matrix for
    each layer, and `ChrononMotionContract.hpp` converts it to the existing
    `chronon_layer_state` records. A connected `ContentHost` supplies the numeric
    opaque content id minted by Chronon; missing ids fail closed instead of being
    hashed. The Chronon side consumes the records through the existing
    `chronon_render_frame_with_layers` entry point in
    `Chronon3d/include/chronon/abi.h`.
    
    The module intentionally does not own an engine or plan handle. The host that
    owns `chronon_engine`/`chronon_plan` can use the thin `ChrononRenderAdapter`, which
    borrows both handles, packs the states and calls `chronon_render_frame_with_layers`.
    The returned `chronon_frame_buffer` remains owned by Chronon3D and is released
    through the adapter; no second renderer or upload path is introduced.
    
    The preview consumer has an explicit `--clean` mode for motion-only inspection.
    It omits HUD, labels, pivots, bounds, strokes and progress indicators. Its strict
    ownership gate also prevents local font/glyph/raster/glow APIs. It does not render
    text pixels; a production canary must be submitted to Chronon3D with a live
    ContentHost and the ADR-032 layer states.
    
    The runtime library remains the only owner of space/time evaluation. Chronon
    still owns content bytes, text layout and rasterization; ChrononTemplate only
    orchestrates the handoff and declares intent. No browser, renderer,
    font system or Windows toolchain is required.
    
    ## Important-phrase style families
    
    RenderingGen names the editorial kind (IMPORTANT_PHRASE);
    `include/chronontemplate/important_phrases/ImportantPhrasePack.hpp` owns how such a phrase looks
    and moves: white Montserrat Bold face with a soft white glow and a slight
    black stroke on the black canvas. `Apple` is the restrained modern
    family and `Didone` the editorial Didone titles. One file per family
    (`ApplePhrasePack.*`, …) on the shared look and motion vocabulary of
    `ImportantPhrasePack.*`, so a pipeline can render one family while the others
    stay ready. (The former `Typewriter` and `Highlight` families were retired:
    their animations rendered unreadable on the installed Vulkan lane.)
    
    The packs are data; `tools/important_phrases/emit_important_phrase_plans.cpp` lowers them to
    `chronon.render-plan.v2` for showcase MP4s on the Vulkan lane (GPU-native text, `require_gpu_native`).
    The GPU lane samples animator properties per run — per-glyph effect is always
    `property(t) * weight(glyph, t)` — so unit-level staging lives in the selector
    // ChrononTemplate — Web Shots Rebuild v1 (C++ base).
    //
    // Port nativo dei 22 shot Python in tools/web_shots/ (groups A-E +
    // web_shot_kit.py) come dati RenderPlan V3 puri.
    // Ogni shot e' una funzione pura dello spec: nessun Pillow, nessun browser,
    // nessuno screenshot caricato come asset. Chronon3D rasterizza, questo pack
    // possiede composizione, layout e timing.
    //
    // Grammatica comune (3.0s, 30fps, 90 frame): piastra -> marker seeded
    // irregolare con core e sweep smoothstep -> camera centrata con push lieve.
    // I dati di marker e le traiettorie restano deterministici per shot.
    // I pannelli tilted (15,16,17,20) usano warp prospettico al render; qui e'
    // dichiarato come tilt statico dei layer + nota nel piano (il renderer
    // applica la prospettiva), cosi' il piano resta valido senza OpenCV.
    //
    // Mappa shot -> Python originale:
    //   A: 07 crt, 08 rainmaking, 09 pinto, 10 tax
    //   B: 03 alexis, 04 corll, 05 economy, 06 thug, 11 acoustic_kitty
    //   C: 12 sabotage, 13 foia, 14 vw, 15 cnbc tilt, 16 nbc tilt
    //   D: 17 guardian tilt, 18 ftx tweet, 19 nyt crazy, 20 indictment tilt, 21 seoul
    //   E: 22 ivie, 23 blackvault, 24 bigfoot
    #ifndef CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_SHOTS_REBUILD_PACK_HPP
    #define CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_SHOTS_REBUILD_PACK_HPP
    
    #include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
    #include <string>
    #include <vector>
    
    namespace chronontemplate::web {

        AlexisArquette = 0,    // 03
        CorllWarehouse,       // 04
        TheyWereEconomy,      // 05
        ThugTeacherQuote,     // 06
        CrtAlcoholHeadline,   // 07
        RainmakingNyt,         // 08
        PintoHighlight,        // 09
        TaxExemptNyt,          // 10
        AcousticKitty,         // 11
        SabotageManualGlow,   // 12
        FoiaFinkelZoom,       // 13
        Vw40Times,            // 14
        CnbcSbfTilt,          // 15
        NbcSwindled8b,        // 16
        GuardianBiggestFrauds,// 17
        FtxTweetCard,         // 18
        NytLookCrazyZoom,     // 19
        IndictmentSummary,    // 20
        GuardianSeoulMissiles,// 21
        IvieFacebook,         // 22
        BlackVaultFoia,       // 23
        BigFootPizza          // 24
    };
    
    [[nodiscard]] const char* webShotName(WebShotId id);
    [[nodiscard]] const char* webShotSource(WebShotId id);
    [[nodiscard]] const char* webShotDescription(WebShotId id);

    /// Funzione pura: stesso input -> stessi byte JSON (RenderPlan V3 completo).
    [[nodiscard]] nlohmann::json buildWebShotPlan(const WebShotSpec& spec);
    
    /// v4: ogni parola entra a runtime con un fade leggero, i marker vengono

    // ChrononTemplate — Web Pages V2 (Complete + Highlight 3D + Long Phrases Blurred).
    //
    // Second-generation native C++ web-page composition pack. Same six-variant
    // web-page grammar (three recipes · two themes) but with the
    // V1 defects fixed and the design reworked:
    //
    //   V1-001  per-glyph headline fold authored rotation in *degrees* (82.0)
    //           while the renderer reads text_animator rotation in *radians*:
    //           the tight producer surface exploded to ~248k px and every video
    //           export threw std::bad_alloc. V2 avoids per-glyph text animators
    //           entirely and uses a layer-level 3D tilt, which also avoids the
    //           cached-text-run bug that left the headline at opacity 0.
    //   V1-002  Complete and Highlight3D both folded the headline, so two of the
    //           three recipes looked identical. V2 Complete uses a soft editorial
    //           fade/rise; only Highlight3D (and the LongPhrase center) folds.
    //   V1-003  flat hierarchy (kicker/meta/byline/sidebar all same voice).
    //           V2 adds an accent kicker bar, a byline+dateline row with share
    //           pills, a lead paragraph voice and numbered sidebar picks.
    //
    // Every plan is a pure function of the spec: complete `chronon.render-plan.v3`
    // objects, identical bytes for identical spec values. 1920x1080 @ 30 fps,
    // no browser, no Python, no Pillow plate involved.
    #ifndef CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_PAGE_V2_PACK_HPP
    #define CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_PAGE_V2_PACK_HPP
    
    #include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
    #include <string>
    #include <vector>
    
    namespace chronontemplate::web {
    
        enum class WebPageV2Theme { Light, Dark };
        enum class WebPageV2Recipe { Complete, Highlight3D, LongPhraseBlurred };
    
        [[nodiscard]] const char* name(WebPageV2Theme theme);
        [[nodiscard]] const char* name(WebPageV2Recipe recipe);
    
        /// One palette per theme; ink vs paper always inverted.
        struct WebPageV2Palette {
            std::string paper{};
            std::string nav{};
            std::string ink{};
            std::string muted{};
            std::string accent{};
            std::string link{};
            std::string rule{};
            std::string panel{};
            std::string panelLine{};
            std::string highlight{};
            std::string body{};
        };
        [[nodiscard]] WebPageV2Palette paletteFor(WebPageV2Theme theme);
    
        struct WebPageV2Spec {
            WebPageV2Theme theme{WebPageV2Theme::Light};
            WebPageV2Recipe recipe{WebPageV2Recipe::Highlight3D};
    
            // chrome
            std::string siteName{"CHRONON NEWS"};
            std::vector<std::string> navLinks{"NBA", "Football", "Business", "Culture"};
            std::string searchHint{"Search"};
            std::string actionLabel{"Subscribe"};
    
            // masthead
            std::string kicker{"NBA"};
            std::string headlineLineOne{};
            std::string headlineLineTwo{};
            std::string byline{};
            std::string dateline{};
            std::string meta{};
    
            // article fields (each vector entry is one pre-wrapped rendered line)
            std::string leadLine{};
            std::vector<std::string> bodyLines{};
            std::vector<std::string> pickTitles{};
    
            // LongPhraseBlurred ingredients
            std::string importantPhrase{};
            std::vector<std::string> contextPhrases{};
    
            std::string outputName{};
            int durationFrames{240};
    
            void validate() const;
    
            [[nodiscard]] std::string planName() const;
            [[nodiscard]] std::string outputStem() const;
        };
    
        /// All six plans (three recipes · two themes) are pure functions of the
        /// spec: the returned document is a complete `chronon.render-plan.v3`
        /// object, identical bytes for identical spec values.
        [[nodiscard]] nlohmann::json buildWebPageV2Plan(const WebPageV2Spec& spec);

        TiltSnapReveal,  // pagina tiltata che scatta in piano (da 15/16/20)
        TimelineDash,    // linea timeline che si disegna + dot ping (da 21 seoul)
        CaptionPopCard   // card bianca che poppa su fondo blur scuro (da 25 pizza)
    };

    # TICKET-CT-PACKS-HELPER-DEDUP-2026-11-22 — split dei pack e helper colore unico
    
    **Stato:** `OPEN`
    **Priorità:** P2
    **Data:** 2026-11-22
    **Owner:** template maintenance
    **Origine:** CT-AUDIT-01
    **Padre:** [TICKET-CT-CLEANUP-2026-11-22](TICKET-CT-CLEANUP-2026-11-22.md)
    
    ## Problema
    
    Quattro pack sono monoliti da oltre 1.100 righe e l'audit ha rilevato helper
    hex/colore duplicati invece di un'unica utility condivisa. Questo rende i fix
    visivi costosi e rischiosi: una modifica al parsing colore va replicata in più
    pack.
    
    ## Evidenza
    
    - `[CODICE]` `src/chronontemplate/backgrounds/BackgroundPack.cpp` — 1.324 righe.
    - `[CODICE]` `src/chronontemplate/map/EditorialMapPack.cpp` — 1.212 righe.
    - `[CODICE]` `src/chronontemplate/web/WebShotsRebuildPack.cpp` — 1.203 righe.
    - `[CODICE]` `src/chronontemplate/multiple_images/MultiImagePack.cpp` — 1.106 righe.
    - `[CODICE]` `BackgroundPack.cpp:107` usa
      `chronon3d::render_plan::parse_hex_color`; l'audit segnala helper equivalenti
      duplicati negli altri pack. Prima dello split va fatto l'inventario esatto:
      ```bash
      rg -n 'hex|parse_color|color_from|rgba' \
        src/chronontemplate/backgrounds/BackgroundPack.cpp \
        src/chronontemplate/map/EditorialMapPack.cpp \
        src/chronontemplate/web/WebShotsRebuildPack.cpp \
        src/chronontemplate/multiple_images/MultiImagePack.cpp
      ```
    
    ## Piano di chiusura
    
    1. **Inventario helper.** Elencare ogni funzione hex/colore e i call site nei
       quattro pack e nel resto di `src/chronontemplate`.
    2. **Un solo owner.** Estrarre il parser in un header/sorgente condiviso sotto
       `src/chronontemplate/core/` (nome da concordare con le convenzioni esistenti)
       e migrare tutti i call site. Nessuna copia locale.
    3. **Split meccanico.** Dividere ogni pack per responsabilità (layout, testo,
       effetti, rendering) in unità più piccole, mantenendo la classe pubblica e
       l'ordine di registrazione; aggiornare il CMake una volta per pack.
    4. **Nessun cambio visivo.** Ogni split deve essere behavior-preserving: stessi
       input, stessi golden/SHA.
    5. **Test dopo ogni pack.** Build e suite template dopo ciascuno split, non
       solo alla fine.
    6. **Documentazione.** Aggiornare il ticket padre con i nuovi file e il mapping
       classe → unità.
    
    ## Gate di accettazione
    
    - [ ] `rg` mostra un solo owner per il parser hex/colore.
    - [ ] Nessun pack supera la soglia concordata (proposta: 800 righe per file).
    - [ ] Build Template verde.
    - [ ] Suite template/golden verde, nessun delta visivo non approvato.
    - [ ] Nessuna API pubblica rimossa o rinominata senza migrazione dei call site.
    
    ## Comandi di verifica
    
    ```bash
    cd ChrononTemplate
    cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
    cmake --build build -j2
    ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
    
    rg -n 'parse_hex_color|hex_to|color_from_hex' src/chronontemplate
    ```
    
    ## Rischi e rollback
    
    - Uno split troppo aggressivo può cambiare l'ordine di registrazione dei pack:
      mantenere l'ordine e verificare i golden.
    - Rollback per pack: ripristinare il file originale e tenere l'helper condiviso
      solo se già migrato e testato.
    
    ## Definition of Done
    
    Helper colore con un solo owner, quattro pack divisi in unità leggibili, build
    e suite template verdi senza delta visivi. La sola estrazione dell'helper non
    chiude il ticket se i monoliti restano.
    # TICKET-CT-CLEANUP-2026-11-22 — monoliths and repository hygiene
    
    **Stato:** `OPEN` (2026-11-22)
    **Owner:** template maintenance
    **Origine:** audit Chronon 2026-11-22, voci CT-AUDIT-01 e REPO-AUDIT-01
    **Ticket figli:** [pack/helper dedup](TICKET-CT-PACKS-HELPER-DEDUP-2026-11-22.md),
    [artifact hygiene](TICKET-REPO-ARTIFACTS-HYGIENE-2026-11-22.md)
    
    ## Problemi
    
    - Monoliti: `BackgroundPack.cpp` (1.324 righe), `EditorialMapPack.cpp`
      (1.212), `WebShotsRebuildPack.cpp` (1.203), `MultiImagePack.cpp` (1.106),
      con helper hex/colore duplicati invece che condivisi in `core/`.
    - Artefatti: 13 `.obj` (~600 KB) tracciati nella root, log di build e file non
      committati; Chronon3d ha log `chronon3d-2026*.log` e PNG
      `RenderingGen_probe*.png` non tracciati; ChrononPlugin ha
      `plugins/maps/assets/maps/cache/pyramid/` non tracciata.
    
    ## Piano
    
    1. Estrarre gli helper colore/hex in un header `core/` unico e far migrare i
       pack; ogni split deve essere meccanico e coperto dai test esistenti.
    2. Verificare l'uso reale dei 13 `.obj` prima di rimuoverli; se sono fixture,
       spostarli sotto `tests/fixtures/` e aggiornare i riferimenti.
    3. Aggiungere al `.gitignore` i log/PNG/cache generati e rimuovere solo gli
       artefatti non tracciati. Nessuna cancellazione di file tracciati senza un
       controllo dei reference.
    4. Non committare build dir o cache; il repo resta riproducibile dai sorgenti.
    
    ## Gate
    
    - [ ] `rg` dimostra che gli helper estratti hanno un solo owner.
    - [ ] Build e suite template PASS dopo ogni split.
    - [ ] `git status` pulito nei quattro repo Chronon (esclusi file live dei job).
    - [ ] Nessun file tracciato rimosso senza riferimento aggiornato.
    - [ ] `[NOT RUN]` al 2026-11-22: nessun build lanciato per RAM occupata.

    ### Image animation starter pack
    
    `tools/important_phrases/build_kinetic_type_editorial_v1.py` authors the reference-inspired
    editorial type family from reusable Chronon3D render-plan primitives. It emits a
    single manifest plus 10 text-motion canaries, eight seeded aurora look canaries,
    five compositional scene-recipe canaries and the 13-scene
    `editorial_typography_gallery_v1`. The authored tokens define a near-black
    canvas, magenta/purple/red/coral aurora colors, bright text and three editorial
    accents. Presets cover a hero scale burst and zoom exit, phrase rise, accented
    word swap, semantic keyword emphasis, luminous underline, same-line slide
    replacement, hero-to-statement handoff, staggered segments, trailing-word
    reveal and scale/blur phrase transitions.
    
    The producer lowers them to ordinary `chronon.render-plan.v3` documents:
    ChrononTemplate owns composition and recipe vocabulary; Chronon3D still owns
    semantic-span layout, text shaping and rasterization. The aurora fields use
    six broad, irregular soft-alpha emitters as moving native image layers.
    `tools/important_phrases/generate_kinetic_type_editorial_textures.py` recreates the deterministic
    palette and accent-light textures. Native per-glyph animators combine scale,
    blur, tracking and fill color; semantic accent spans drive a synchronized
    colored light layer. The `Design` gallery beat uses three animated color spans
    to approximate a red-to-magenta gradient while staying on the Vulkan text
    path. Underlines use a Vulkan-native rounded stroke with an overshoot draw and
    soft afterglow. Hero words may crop intentionally, while sentence lines retain
    the native shrink-only fit contract.
    
    Generate plans and run the deterministic/safe-area contract tests:
    
    ```shell
    python3 tools/important_phrases/generate_kinetic_type_editorial_textures.py
    python3 tools/important_phrases/build_kinetic_type_editorial_v1.py --out build/kinetic_type_editorial_v1
    python3 tools/important_phrases/test_kinetic_type_editorial_v1.py
    ```
    
    Validate all generated plans with the local Chronon3D CLI, or render a single
    scene with Vulkan to raw NV12 frames, then encode the final MP4 with NVIDIA
    NVENC (preview profile and a 512 MiB framebuffer-pool retention budget):
    
    ```shell
    python3 tools/important_phrases/build_kinetic_type_editorial_v1.py \
      --out build/kinetic_type_editorial_v1 --validate-only \
      --cli ../Chronon3d/build/chronon/linux-video-fast-dev/apps/chronon3d_cli/chronon3d_cli
    python3 tools/important_phrases/build_kinetic_type_editorial_v1.py \
      --out build/kinetic_type_editorial_v1 --render --scene canary_text_word_pop_focus \
      --cli ../Chronon3d/build/chronon/linux-video-fast-dev/apps/chronon3d_cli/chronon3d_cli
    ```
    
    Use `--render-all` for the complete 24-plan canary set. Vulkan exports start in
    sequential bounded-frame renderer processes; a failed range is bisected until
    it passes. Raw frame ranges are joined and encoded once with NVENC at constant
    30 fps. Use `--render-from <plan>`
    to resume a stopped batch after the last verified plan. The
    pack's contract verifies stable ids, finite bounded
    parameters, keyframe/lifetime integrity, UTF-8 semantic spans, safe-area bounds,
    scene handoff overlap, palette/type/background coverage and renderer-native
    plan schemas. A renderer validation or canary establishes contract support,
    not pixel equivalence to an unprovided reference-video frame.

    -// ChrononTemplate — Web Headline Highlight pack.
    -//
    -// Native C++ recreations of six editorial highlighter looks seen in the
    -// supplied reference frames: a statement page whose headline phrase sits under
    -// a coral marker, a marker sweep over an italic serif phrase on lined paper,
    -// a stepped yellow highlight over a serif headline, a breaking-news page with
    -// a red kicker bar and a ticker tape, a live-blog feed whose latest entry is
    -// marked, and a centered quote card with a coral key-phrase highlight. Every
    -// pixel is authored as render-plan V3 data (text and shape layers with camera
    -// animation); no browser, no Python and no Pillow plate is involved. Chronon3D
    -// rasterizes; this pack owns the design vocabulary, the layout and the timing.
    -//
    -// The six recipes share one grammar: the highlighter is the point of the
    -// shot and the supporting copy is quieter around it.
    -//
    -//   HeadlineHighlightRecipe::StatementPage   full statement page (nav, kicker,
    -//                                            highlighted headline phrase,
    -//                                            dateline, serif body)
    -//   HeadlineHighlightRecipe::MarkerSweep     lined paper, italic serif phrase,
    -//                                            yellow marker band sweeping in
    -//   HeadlineHighlightRecipe::SteppedHighlight serif headline with stepped
    -//                                            yellow blocks behind the lead
    -//                                            lines and a red-bullet kicker
    -//   HeadlineHighlightRecipe::BreakingTicker  dark breaking-news page (red
    -//                                            kicker bar, stepped headline
    -//                                            highlight, sliding ticker tape)
    -//   HeadlineHighlightRecipe::LiveBlogFeed    live-blog feed (LIVE dot,
    -//                                            timestamped entries, marker band
    -//                                            on the latest entry)
    -//   HeadlineHighlightRecipe::QuoteCard       centered quote card (serif
    -//                                            italic quote, coral key-phrase
    -//                                            highlight, attribution)
    -//
    -// The highlight geometry is estimated from the authored copy with the pack's
    -// deterministic width table: blocks are composition intent, not glyph-exact
    -// coverage. Where a reference band is hand-drawn (the marker sweep's slanted
    -// ends) the pack approximates it with stacked rectangles rather than claiming
    -// optical-identical ink.
    -#ifndef CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_HEADLINE_HIGHLIGHT_PACK_HPP
    -#define CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_HEADLINE_HIGHLIGHT_PACK_HPP
    -
    -#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
    -#include <string>
    -#include <vector>
    -
    -namespace chronontemplate::web {
    -
    -    enum class HeadlineHighlightRecipe : unsigned char {
    -        StatementPage,
    -        MarkerSweep,
    -        SteppedHighlight,
    -        BreakingTicker,
    -        LiveBlogFeed,
    -        QuoteCard
    -    };
    -
    -    [[nodiscard]] const char* name(HeadlineHighlightRecipe recipe);
    -
    -    struct WebHeadlineHighlightSpec {
    -        HeadlineHighlightRecipe recipe{HeadlineHighlightRecipe::StatementPage};
    -
    -        // shared copy
    -        std::string kicker{};                    ///< "Announcements", "AI • META", ...
    -        std::vector<std::string> headlineLines{};///< rendered headline lines (1..4)
    -        std::string highlightText{};             ///< phrase covered by the highlighter
    -        std::string dateline{};                  ///< centered date under the headline
    -        std::vector<std::string> bodyLines{};    ///< serif body copy (1..8 lines),
    -                                                 ///< or live-blog entries (2..4)
    -
    -        // statement-page chrome
    -        std::string siteName{"CHRONON NEWS"};
    -        std::vector<std::string> navLinks{"Research", "Policy", "Pronouncements"};
    -
    -        // marker-sweep phrase (recipe two); italic serif on lined paper
    -        std::string phrase{};                    ///< the marked phrase, e.g. "one company"
    -
    -        // breaking-ticker tape (recipe four); one muted line sliding in
    -        std::string tickerText{};                ///< e.g. "Markets rally as ..."
    -
    -        // live-blog feed (recipe five); bodyLines are the entry texts and
    -        // entryTimes carries one short timestamp per entry, in order
    -        std::vector<std::string> entryTimes{};
    -
    -        // quote card (recipe six); centered serif italic lines plus credit
    -        std::vector<std::string> quoteLines{};   ///< the quote, 1..3 lines
    -        std::string attribution{};               ///< e.g. "Ada Lovelace"
    -        std::string source{};                    ///< e.g. "The Interview, Jun 2026"
    -
    -        // palette overrides; empty keeps the recipe's authored colors
    -        std::string paperColor{};
    -        std::string inkColor{};
    -        std::string highlightColor{};
    -
    -        std::string outputName{};  ///< mp4 stem; empty falls back to the plan name
    -        int durationFrames{180};
    -
    -        void validate() const;
    -
    -        [[nodiscard]] std::string planName() const;

    // ChrononTemplate — Modern Documentary pack.
    //
    // Five native RenderPlan V3 looks distilled from the supplied modern
    // documentary references:
    //
    //   VoxHighlight   paper article, left-anchored multiply highlighter, subject
    //                  cutout, rack focus and floating dust.
    //   SplitGlitch    torn split composition, glowing energy divider, UI card in
    //                  Z-space with chromatic/mesh/slice glitch treatment.
    //   MacroUiRain    macro comment UI, typewriter sentence, layered crowd
    //                  silhouettes and a banknote particle rain with HUD.
    //   KineticType    four 3D typographic beats, left-to-right bars and a
    //                  whip-pan camera with a 180-degree temporal shutter.
    //   VhsCarousel    CRT frame, spring-overshoot logo carousel, hot title and
    //                  analog scanline/chroma wear.
    //
    // Every look is authored as ordinary `chronon.render-plan.v3` data. Chronon3D
    // owns rasterization, effects, camera sampling and encoding; this module owns
    // the design vocabulary and timing. No browser, DOM or live JS is involved.
    //
    // The pack deliberately uses the renderer's existing primitives:
    //   * multiply blend + shape scale/position tracks (highlighter),
    //   * camera_samples with thin-lens DoF (rack focus),
    //   * text_animators + a character selector (typewriter),
    //   * temporal_motion_blur + per-frame camera_samples (whip pan),
    //   * chromatic_aberration, mesh_warp, scanlines, retro_tv, roughen_edges,
    //     lens_distortion, glow/bloom and directional_blur (analog/UI wear),
    //   * particle_emitter sprite, rotation and angular_velocity fields.
    //
    // The banknote rain is a 2.5D environment emitter: it uses the existing
    // per-particle sprite rotation and fake depth/DoF fields. It is not a claim of
    // a full six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body particle solver.
    #ifndef CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_MODERN_DOCUMENTARY_PACK_HPP
    #define CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_MODERN_DOCUMENTARY_PACK_HPP
    
    #include <array>
    #include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
    #include <string>
    
    namespace chronontemplate::web {
    
    enum class ModernDocumentaryRecipe : unsigned char {
        VoxHighlight,
        SplitGlitch,
        MacroUiRain,
        KineticType,
        VhsCarousel
    };
    
    [[nodiscard]] const char* modernDocumentaryName(ModernDocumentaryRecipe recipe);
    [[nodiscard]] std::array<ModernDocumentaryRecipe, 5> allModernDocumentaryRecipes();
    
    struct ModernDocumentarySpec {
        ModernDocumentaryRecipe recipe{ModernDocumentaryRecipe::VoxHighlight};
        int durationFrames{150};  // 5 s at 30 fps
        int fps{30};
        std::string outputName{};
    
        void validate() const;
        [[nodiscard]] std::string planName() const;
        [[nodiscard]] std::string outputStem() const;
    };
    
    /// Complete `chronon.render-plan.v3` document for one look.
    [[nodiscard]] nlohmann::json buildModernDocumentaryPlan(const ModernDocumentarySpec& spec);
    
    }  // namespace chronontemplate::web
    
    #endif  // CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_MODERN_DOCUMENTARY_PACK_HPP

    /// All line measurements come from Chronon3D's HarfBuzz shaping result.
    /// A callback keeps the template library renderer-link-free; production code
    /// should bind it to FontEngine::shape_text (see chrononTextShaper).
    using TextShaper = std::function<std::optional<chronon3d::GlyphRun>(std::string_view)>;
    
    struct WebTextLine {
        std::string text;
        std::size_t sourceBegin{0};
        std::size_t sourceEnd{0};
        float x{0.f};
        float top{0.f};
        float baseline{0.f};
        float width{0.f};
        float ascent{0.f};
        float descent{0.f};
        float lineHeight{0.f};
        chronon3d::GlyphRun shaped{};
    };
    
    struct WebTextLayout {
        std::string source;
        std::string fontPath;
        float fontSize{0.f};
        std::vector<WebTextLine> lines;
        float width{0.f};
        float height{0.f};
    };
    
    /// A single physical-line segment of a semantic span, in pixel coordinates.
    struct WebTextSegment {
        std::size_t lineIndex{0};
        float x{0.f};
        float y{0.f};
        float width{0.f};
        float height{0.f};
        std::size_t sourceBegin{0};
        std::size_t sourceEnd{0};
    };
    
    /// Wraps at whitespace using exact shaped candidate widths. The input's byte
    /// offsets are retained so spans remain stable across UTF-8 text and wrapping.
    [[nodiscard]] WebTextLayout layoutWebText(std::string_view text, float x, float y,
                                               float maxWidth, float lineSpacing,
                                               const std::string& fontPath, float fontSize,
                                               const TextShaper& shape);
    
    /// Maps a source byte interval to one segment per intersected visual line.
    /// Glyph clusters, rather than estimated character widths, determine x bounds.
    [[nodiscard]] std::vector<WebTextSegment> resolveWebTextSpan(
        const WebTextLayout& layout, std::size_t byteStart, std::size_t byteEnd);
    
    /// Convenience adapter for production callers that link Chronon3D.
    [[nodiscard]] inline TextShaper chrononTextShaper(
        const chronon3d::FontEngine& engine, chronon3d::FontSpec font, float size,
        chronon3d::TextShaping shaping = {}) {
        return [&engine, font = std::move(font), size, shaping = std::move(shaping)](std::string_view text) {
            return engine.shape_text(text, font, size, shaping);
        };
    }

        // 1:1 wire->px mapping: 540/tan(25deg) = 1158.06 (calibration renders
        // confirm rects land on authored pixels; -1320 scaled 0.877 to center).
    
        void checksPlanEnvelope(const json& plan, const std::string& jobId, int duration,
                                bool expectCamera) {
            check(plan.at("schema") == "chronon.render-plan.v3" && plan.at("version") == 3,
                  "the plan is render-plan V3");
            check(plan.at("job_id") == jobId, "the job id follows the recipe identity");
            const auto& canvas = plan.at("canvas");
            check(canvas.at("width") == 1920 && canvas.at("height") == 1080,
                  "the canvas is 1920x1080");
            check(canvas.at("fps_num") == 30 && canvas.at("fps_den") == 1,
                  "the canvas is 30 fps");
            check(canvas.at("duration_frames") == duration,
                  "the canvas carries the authored duration");
            check(plan.at("output").at("format") == "mp4" &&
                      plan.at("output").at("codec") == "h264",
                  "the output is H.264 mp4");
            check(!plan.contains("camera_samples"),
                  "the plan does not carry obsolete camera samples");
            if (expectCamera) {
                check(plan.contains("camera"), "the plan declares a camera");
                const auto& camera = plan.at("camera");
                check(camera.at("type") == "perspective", "the camera is perspective");
                chrononmotion_test::checkNear(camera.at("position")[2].get<float>(),
                                             -1158.06f, 0.01f,
                                             "the camera gives 1:1 wire to pixel mapping");
            } else {
                check(!plan.contains("camera"),
                      "the rebuild plan is camera-less screen-space 2D");
            }
        }
    
        const json* findLayer(const json& plan, const std::string& id) {
            for (const auto& layer : plan.at("layers"))
                if (layer.value("id", std::string{}) == id) return &layer;
            return nullptr;
        }
    
        void checksLayerContract(const json& plan) {
            std::set<std::string> ids;
            bool hasText = false;
            for (const auto& layer : plan.at("layers")) {
                check(ids.insert(layer.at("id").get<std::string>()).second,
                      "layer ids are unique inside the plan");
                const std::string type = layer.at("type").get<std::string>();
                if (type == "color") {
                    check(layer.value("screen_space", false),
                          "a full-bleed color plate is screen-space");
                    check(layer.at("size")[0] == 1920 && layer.at("size")[1] == 1080,
                          "the screen-space plate covers the canvas");
                }
                if (type == "text") {
                    hasText = true;
                    check(layer.contains("style"), "a text layer carries a style block");
                    const auto& style = layer.at("style");
                    check(!style.contains("fit_mode") && !style.contains("text_align"),
                          "text uses the renderer's measured-box contract, not fit/align overrides");
                    check(layer.at("size")[0].get<float>() >= 60.f,
                          "the text box is measured from the copy");
                    check(std::isfinite(layer.at("position")[0].get<float>()) &&
                              std::isfinite(layer.at("position")[1].get<float>()),
                          "the text position is finite");
                }
            }
            check(hasText, "every web shot authors at least one text layer");
        }

        const nlohmann::json* findLayer(const nlohmann::json& plan, const std::string& id) {
            for (const auto& layer : plan["layers"]) {
                if (layer.value("id", "") == id) return &layer;
            }
            return nullptr;
        }
    
        const nlohmann::json& layer(const nlohmann::json& plan, const std::string& id) {
            const auto* found = findLayer(plan, id);
            assert(found != nullptr && "missing expected layer");
            return *found;
        }
    
        int layerIndex(const nlohmann::json& plan, const std::string& id) {
            int index = 0;
            for (const auto& layer : plan["layers"]) {
                if (layer.value("id", "") == id) return index;
                ++index;
            }
            return -1;
        }
    
        // Text is emitted centre-relative; shapes are still in canvas coordinates
        // at this stage. Normalise both to the 1920x1080 canvas before comparing.
        double canvasCenterX(const nlohmann::json& layer) {
            const auto& position = layer.at("position");
            return layer.value("type", "") == "text"
                ? position[0].get<double>() + 960.0
                : position[0].get<double>();
        }
    
        double canvasTop(const nlohmann::json& layer) {
            const auto& position = layer.at("position");
            const auto& size = layer.at("size");
            const double centerY = layer.value("type", "") == "text"
                ? position[1].get<double>() + 540.0
                : position[1].get<double>();
            return centerY - size[1].get<double>() * 0.5;
        }
    
        void assertCentredPage(const nlohmann::json& plan) {
            const auto& nav = layer(plan, "nav_bar");
            assert(std::fabs(canvasCenterX(nav) - 960.0) < 0.01);
            assert(std::fabs(canvasTop(nav)) < 0.01);
            assert(std::fabs(canvasCenterX(layer(plan, "footer_rule")) - 960.0) < 0.01);
    
            const auto& headline = layer(plan, "headline_line_1");
            const auto& lineTwo = layer(plan, "headline_line_2");
            const double headlineLeft = canvasCenterX(headline) - headline["size"][0].get<double>() * 0.5;
            const double lineTwoLeft = canvasCenterX(lineTwo) - lineTwo["size"][0].get<double>() * 0.5;
            assert(std::fabs(headlineLeft - lineTwoLeft) < 0.01);
            assert(headlineLeft >= 150.0 && headlineLeft <= 166.0);
    
            const auto& sidebar = layer(plan, "sidebar_panel");
            assert(std::fabs(canvasCenterX(sidebar) + sidebar["size"][0].get<double>() * 0.5 - 1770.0) < 0.01);
        }
    
        void assertVerticalOrder(const nlohmann::json& plan) {

        void assertLongPhraseOrder(const nlohmann::json& plan) {
    // The paper-reference contract: five stable recipes, native V3 envelopes,
    // deterministic plans, the native highlighter bands and fail-closed specs.
    #include "chronontemplate/web/WebPaperReferencePack.hpp"
    
    #include "motion_check.hpp"
    
    #include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
    
    #include <cmath>
    #include <set>
    #include <string>
    #include <vector>
    
    using json = nlohmann::json;
    using namespace chronontemplate::web;
    using chrononmotion_test::check;
    using chrononmotion_test::section;
    
    namespace {
    
    const json* layerById(const json& plan, const std::string& id) {
        for (const auto& layer : plan.at("layers"))
            if (layer.value("id", std::string{}) == id) return &layer;
        return nullptr;
    }
    
    /// Keyframe value of a track; -1 when the layer has no such track.
    float keyValue(const json& layer, const std::string& property, bool first) {
        if (!layer.contains("animation")) return -1.f;
        for (const auto& track : layer.at("animation").at("tracks")) {
            if (track.value("property", std::string{}) != property) continue;
            const auto& keys = track.at("keyframes");
            return (first ? keys.front() : keys.back()).at("value").get<float>();
        }
        return -1.f;
    }
    
    /// Authored left edge in canvas px. Images are centre-relative; shapes are
    /// absolute top-down in this pack.
    float leftEdge(const json& layer) {
        const float centre = layer.at("position")[0].get<float>();
        return (layer.value("type", "") == "shape" ? centre : centre + 960.f) -
               layer.at("size")[0].get<float>() * 0.5f;
    }
    
    void checksEnvelope(const json& plan, const std::string& jobId, int duration) {
        check(plan.at("schema") == "chronon.render-plan.v3" && plan.at("version") == 3,
              "the plan is render-plan V3");
        check(plan.at("job_id") == jobId, "the job id follows the recipe identity");
        const auto& canvas = plan.at("canvas");
        check(canvas.at("width") == 1920 && canvas.at("height") == 1080,
              "the canvas is 1920x1080");
        check(canvas.at("fps_num") == 30 && canvas.at("fps_den") == 1,
              "the canvas is 30 fps");
        check(canvas.at("duration_frames") == duration,
              "the canvas carries the authored duration");
        check(plan.at("output").at("format") == "mp4" &&
                  plan.at("output").at("codec") == "h264",
              "the output is H.264 mp4");
        check(plan.contains("camera") && plan.at("camera").at("type") == "perspective",
              "the plan declares a perspective camera");
        check(!plan.contains("camera_samples"),
              "the plan does not carry obsolete camera samples");
    }
    
    void checksLayers(const json& plan) {
        std::set<std::string> ids;
        for (const auto& layer : plan.at("layers")) {
            check(ids.insert(layer.at("id").get<std::string>()).second,
                  "layer ids are unique inside the plan");
            check(layer.at("position").is_array() && layer.at("position").size() >= 2,
                  "every layer has a position");
            if (layer.at("type") == "image") {
                check(layer.contains("asset") && !layer.at("asset").get<std::string>().empty(),
                      "an image layer names its content asset");
            }
        }
        check(plan.at("layers").size() >= 2, "the recipe composes a real scene");
    }
    
    void checksRecipes() {
        section("paper reference recipes");
        const auto recipes = allPaperReferenceRecipes();
        check(recipes.size() == 5, "all five reference recipes are registered");
        const std::vector<std::string> expected = {
            "web_ref_newspaper_tilt", "web_ref_torn_strip", "web_ref_blurred_evidence",
            "web_ref_bridge_collage", "web_ref_book_highlight"};
        std::set<std::string> names;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < recipes.size(); ++i) {
            check(std::string(paperReferenceName(recipes[i])) == expected[i],
                  "the recipe name is stable and ordered");
            check(names.insert(paperReferenceName(recipes[i])).second,
                  "every recipe has a unique stable name");
    
            PaperReferenceSpec spec;
            spec.recipe = recipes[i];
            const json plan = buildPaperReferencePlan(spec);
            checksEnvelope(plan, spec.planName(), 180);
            checksLayers(plan);
            check(plan.at("output").at("path") == spec.planName() + ".mp4",
                  "the output stem follows the plan name");
            check(buildPaperReferencePlan(spec).dump() == plan.dump(),
                  "the emitted plan is deterministic");
        }
    }

                }

            check(hasText, "every web shot authors at least one text layer");

## User

Questo stile visivo — reso celebre su YouTube da canali documentaristici e d'inchiesta come *Vox*, *Fern*, *LEMMiNO* e *MagnatesMedia* — combina **grafica 2D ad alta risoluzione**, **movimenti di camera in spazio 3D** e **effetti ottici** (sfocatura e vignettatura) per trasformare semplici documenti o articoli di giornale in sequenze cinematografiche.

Analizzando i due fotogrammi, l'effetto è composto da **5 livelli sovrapposti**:

1. **Testo ricreato in alta definizione:** Invece di usare screenshot sgranati di PDF o pagine web, il testo viene spesso riscritto da zero su uno sfondo bianco/avorio per restare nitidissimo anche con zoom spinti.


2. **Texture carta e vignettatura:** Sopra lo sfondo viene applicata una texture di carta molto leggera e una forte vignettatura scura ai bordi per concentrare l'occhio dello spettatore al centro.


3. **Evidenziatore organico animato:** Le strisce verdi e gialle non sono semplici rettangoli piatti, ma tratti leggermente irregolari che si srotolano da sinistra a destra sincronizzati con la voce narrante.


4. **Inclinazione e movimento in 3D:** Il foglio non è piatto rispetto allo schermo, ma ruotato nello spazio 3D (asse X, Y e Z) mentre una camera virtuale scorre lentamente lungo le righe.


5. **Profondità di campo (Depth of Field):** Le righe in primo piano o sullo sfondo sono sfocate, lasciando a fuoco solo la frase che si sta leggendo in quel momento.



---

### Come realizzarlo in Adobe After Effects (Metodo Standard)

After Effects è il software più usato per ottenere questo risultato preciso:

1. **Prepara il documento:** Crea una composizione (es. 1920x1080 o 4K) con un livello tinta unita bianco sporco (`#F4F3EF`) e incolla o riscrivi il testo. Aggiungi sopra una texture di carta in modalità di fusione **Moltiplica (Multiply)** con opacità al 10-15%.
2. **Crea l'evidenziatore animato:**
* Seleziona lo **Strumento Penna** (senza riempimento, solo traccia spessa circa 35-45 px, colore giallo o verde acceso) e traccia una linea sopra la riga di testo.


* Imposta il metodo di fusione del livello forma su **Moltiplica (Multiply)** in modo che il testo nero resti perfettamente leggibile sotto il colore.


* Aggiungi l'effetto **Taglia tracciati (Trim Paths)** e anima il parametro *Fine (End)* da `0%` a `100%` in circa 0,5–1 secondo.
* Per renderlo simile a un vero pennarello, applica l'effetto **Bordi frastagliati (Roughen Edges)** con valori bassi (es. *Bordo* a 3-5).




3. **Attiva lo spazio 3D e la Camera:**
* Pre-componi il foglio + testo + evidenziatori in un unico livello e attiva l'icona del **cubo 3D** sul livello.
* Crea un nuovo livello **Videocamera (Camera)** (lente da 35mm o 50mm) e ruota il livello del foglio sugli assi X, Y e Z per ottenere l'inclinazione diagonale del secondo screenshot.


* Anima la posizione della camera con un movimento lento e continuo (*Easy Ease*).


4. **Aggiungi la sfocatura ottica e la vignettatura:**
* Nelle impostazioni della Videocamera, attiva **Profondità di campo (Depth of Field)**, regola la *Distanza di messa a fuoco* sulla riga principale e alza l'*Apertura* finché i bordi del testo non risultano morbidamente sfocati.


* Crea un **Livello di regolazione (Adjustment Layer)** in cima a tutto, applica l'effetto **Lumetri Color** (o *CC Vignette*) per scurire pesantemente i quattro angoli e aggiungi un pizzico di **Disturbo (Noise)** (2-3%) per uniformare l'immagine.





---

### Alternative più rapide (senza After Effects)

* **DaVinci Resolve (Gratuita e molto vicina ad After Effects):** Nella pagina *Fusion* puoi usare il nodo **Image Plane 3D** collegato a **Camera 3D** e **Renderer 3D** per inclinare il documento e attivare il *Depth of Field*. Per l'evidenziatore basta un nodo *Background* colorato con una maschera rettangolare animata in modalità *Multiply*.
* **Adobe Premiere Pro:** Puoi usare l'effetto **3D Base (Basic 3D)** per inclinare il foglio, l'effetto **Pulizia lineare (Linear Wipe)** su un livello colorato impostato su *Moltiplica* per l'evidenziatore, e una maschera sfumata su un livello di regolazione con *Sfocatura gaussiana* per simulare la profondità di campo.
* **CapCut Desktop:** Importa l'immagine del documento, usa l'animazione/regolazione **3D** o i keyframe di scala/rotazione, aggiungi un adesivo/forma rettangolare gialla con metodo di fusione **Scurisci/Moltiplica** animata con tendina da sinistra a destra, e applica gli effetti **Vignettatura** e **Sfocatura bordi** dalla libreria effetti.

**Un dettaglio fondamentale per la resa finale:** nei video di questo tipo l'animazione visiva funziona grazie al **sound design**. Abbina sempre all'apparizione del foglio un leggero fruscio di carta (*paper rustle*) e al passaggio dell'evidenziatore il suono soffuso di un pennarello su carta (*marker stroke*).

    # Google Drive
    
    Use this Google Drive skill to find files, organize them in folders, manage sharing, make copies, export or delete files, and check revision history.
    
    To read or edit the contents of a Google Doc, Sheet, or Slides presentation, use the corresponding skill in the same Google Drive plugin. If you need to find the file first, use the Drive skill to locate it. If the user has already identified the file, go directly to the skill for that file type.
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Ground the target file first.
    - If the user did not provide an exact file URL or ID, use Google Drive search, recent files, folder listing, or metadata reads to identify the right file.
    - If the request starts as "find X and then update it," do the Drive discovery step first instead of guessing the target.
    
    2. Use this skill for actions on Drive files and folders.
    - Use the base workflow for search, fetch, recent files, folders, sharing, copying, deleting, exporting, revision history, file moves, and other file-lifecycle work that is not primarily about editing Docs, Sheets, or Slides content.
    - For version-history requests, including "previous version," "revision history," "what changed since the last version," or "compare to the prior revision," ground the file, fetch the current content, use `list_file_revisions`, fetch the immediately previous revision or the user-named revision with `fetch_file_revision`, then compare the fetched revision against the current content. Do not say previous versions are unsupported until you have checked whether revision tools are available for the target file.
    - For file move requests, ground the source file and target folder, read the file metadata including its current parents, then use `update_file` with `addParents` for the target folder and `removeParents` for only the verified source parent or parents that should no longer contain it. Preserve unrelated parents, and verify the move by reading metadata or listing the target folder before the final response.
    - Before any export or raw-file fetch, read or reuse Drive metadata so the MIME type and Google Drive URL are known. Use `export_file` only to convert a native Google Doc, Sheet, or Slide into an explicitly requested format; it returns an authenticated file reference, not inline bytes or base64. Google limits `files.export` responses to **10 MB**; oversized exports fail rather than returning truncated content. For a larger native PDF, use `download_file(id=file_id, mime_type="application/pdf")` when the streaming action is available. It calls Google's `files.download` API and returns a top-level materializable `file_uri`. Once `download_file` is unavailable and canonical `fetch` uses that streamed download path, use `fetch(url=google_drive_url, download_raw_file=True, raw_export_mime_type="application/pdf")` instead. A native-file `fetch` that still uses `files.export` cannot bypass the 10 MB limit. For PDFs, images, ZIPs, Office files, recordings, and other stored, non-native files, use `fetch(url=google_drive_url, download_raw_file=True)`. Use only the authenticated top-level `file_uri` or materialized `workspace_path`; never request inline base64 unless an existing caller explicitly opts into bounded legacy compatibility. Use `fetch` without `download_raw_file` for bounded, best-effort readable text. Do not retry `export_file` after metadata shows a non-native MIME type.
    
    3. For work on a file’s contents, use the Docs, Sheets, or Slides skill for that file type. To add, reply to, or resolve comments, use google-drive-comments.
    - Drive, Docs, Sheets, or Slides comment creation, comment replies, comment resolution, or review-by-comments: use [google-drive-comments](../google-drive-comments/SKILL.md).
    - Google Docs net-new creation, content summary, revision planning, prose rewriting, or section edits: use [google-docs](../google-docs/SKILL.md).
    - Google Sheets creation, local spreadsheet import, range inspection, table cleanup, data restructuring, formula design or repair, chart creation or repair, or batch updates: use [google-sheets](../google-sheets/SKILL.md).
    - Google Slides deck summary, content edits, new deck creation, local presentation import, visual cleanup, structural repair, or template migration: use [google-slides](../google-slides/SKILL.md).
    
    ## Routing Rules
    
    - If the request is ambiguous between Drive and a file-type surface, use the artifact itself as the tie-breaker:
      - Doc -> Docs skill
      - Sheet -> Sheets skill
      - Deck -> Slides skill
    - If the user wants to find a file and then edit it, do both in one flow: Drive for discovery, then the file-type skill for the edit.
    - If the user wants a Google Workspace outcome but has not named a file type yet, start with Drive discovery instead of asking them to choose among separate Google plugins.
    - If the user asks to create a new Google Doc, route to the Docs skill; it owns the mandatory local `.docx` -> native Google Docs import workflow and the explicit-user-override boundary. Do not create a blank Google Doc directly from this router.
    - If the user asks to import a local `.docx` into Google Docs, route to the Docs skill and use its native conversion workflow. Preserve the source file type only when the user explicitly asks for that.
    - If the user asks to create a new Google Sheet, route to the Sheets skill. The Sheets skill should prefer the `[@spreadsheets](plugin://spreadsheets@openai-primary-runtime)` plugin or `$Excel` skill to create a local `.xlsx`, then import it as native Google Sheets.
    - If the user asks to import a local `.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.ods`, `.csv`, or `.tsv` into Google Sheets, route to the Sheets skill and use native Google Sheets conversion by default. Preserve the source file type only when the user explicitly asks for that.
    - If the user asks to create a new Google Slides deck, route to the Slides skill; it owns the mandatory local `.pptx` -> native Google Slides import workflow and the explicit-user-override boundary. Do not create a blank Google Slides deck directly from this router.
    - If the user asks to import a local `.ppt`, `.pptx`, or `.odp` into Google Slides, route to the Slides skill and use its native conversion workflow. Preserve the source file type only when the user explicitly asks for that.

For a larger native PDF, prefer the currently available streaming `download_file(id=file_id, mime_type="application/pdf")`; after canonical `fetch` adopts the same streamed download path and `download_file` is removed, use `fetch(url=google_drive_url, download_raw_file=True, raw_export_mime_type="application/pdf")`. Stored, non-native PDFs, images, ZIPs, CSVs, Office files, audio, and video use `fetch(url=google_drive_url, download_raw_file=True)`. Use the returned top-level `file_uri` or its authenticated, materialized `workspace_path`; do not expose inline binary, base64, or a bearer URL.     ## Write Safety
    
    - Preserve the user's existing file organization, sharing state, and target artifact unless the request clearly asks to change them.

    - For any file import or explicit direct create that returns a user-facing Google Workspace link, wait for the write action to complete and verify the created file with connector readback or Drive metadata readback before returning the URL. Use only a URL or id observed from the completed connector result or readback; never synthesize or predict the URL.

## Assistant

I due screenshot mostrano due scene diverse: (1) documento archivistico fotografato, inclinato, con carta calda, vignetta e sfocatura; (2) pagina digitale “Pill Press Threat”, frontale, testo nitido e due highlight verdi/gialli con bordi morbidi. Non sono cinque layer identici in entrambi: nel secondo non vedo una rotazione 3D marcata né una vera carta fotografica. Imposto la prima verifica come due still native 854×480, senza inventare immagini o contenuti aggiuntivi; per il video collegato verifico prima che sia davvero il soggetto da ricreare, perché il nome è “Gianni De Gennaro” e non coincide con gli screenshot sul fentanyl.

    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
    
    # ChrononTemplate — the composition/template module of the Chronon stack.
    #
    # It is the sibling of ChrononMotion, whose motion primitives it consumes, and
    # of Chronon3d, the renderer. This module owns recipes: composition presets and
    # the social/web template catalog. It owns no renderer, no content bytes and no
    # font layout — text and image identifiers stay opaque `ContentRef`s.
    #
    # `include/chrononmotion/templates/` is deliberately part of this module: the
    # template catalog was moved out of the motion core and keeps its namespace.
    
    project(ChrononTemplate
            VERSION 0.1.0
            DESCRIPTION "Composition presets and templates built on ChrononMotion"
            LANGUAGES CXX)
    
    option(CHRONONTEMPLATE_BUILD_TESTS "Build the ChrononTemplate test binaries" ${PROJECT_IS_TOP_LEVEL})
    option(CHRONONTEMPLATE_WERROR "Turn compiler warnings into errors" OFF)
    option(CHRONONTEMPLATE_BUILD_LIVE_ADAPTER_TEST "Link the live adapter test against Chronon3D" OFF)
    set(CHRONONTEMPLATE_NLOHMANN_JSON_INCLUDE_DIR
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../Chronon3d/vcpkg_installed/linux-fast-dev/x64-linux/include"
        CACHE PATH "Directory containing nlohmann/json.hpp")
    find_path(CHRONONTEMPLATE_NLOHMANN_JSON_DIR nlohmann/json.hpp
              HINTS "${CHRONONTEMPLATE_NLOHMANN_JSON_INCLUDE_DIR}")
    if(NOT CHRONONTEMPLATE_NLOHMANN_JSON_DIR)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "ChrononTemplate native plan builders require nlohmann/json.hpp")
    endif()
    set(CHRONONTEMPLATE_EDITORIAL_RENDERER_CLI "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../Chronon3d/build/chronon/linux-video-test/apps/chronon3d_cli/chronon3d_cli"
        CACHE FILEPATH "Chronon3D CLI used to validate the editorial benchmark plans")
    set(CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_LIBRARY "" CACHE FILEPATH
        "Chronon3D library used by the optional live adapter test")
    # ── Renderer checkout: the one explicit Chronon3D dependency ─────────────────
    #
    # A headless template build still reads the renderer's neutral value types
    # (`chronon/abi.h`, `chronon3d/graphics/*`) from this checkout. It is a
    # checkout dependency, not a silent sibling-folder assumption: every
    # `../Chronon3d` reference below goes through this variable, and a missing
    # checkout fails here with the fix instead of a stray header error later.
    if(EXISTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../Chronon3d")
        set(CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DEFAULT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../Chronon3d")
    elseif(EXISTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../Chronon3D")
        set(CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DEFAULT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../Chronon3D")
    else()
        set(CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DEFAULT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../Chronon3d")
    endif()
    set(CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DIR "${CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DEFAULT}"
        CACHE PATH "Chronon3D checkout providing chronon/abi.h and chronon3d/graphics/*")
    if(NOT EXISTS "${CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DIR}/include/chronon/abi.h")
        message(FATAL_ERROR
                "ChrononTemplate needs chronon/abi.h from a Chronon3D checkout at "
                "'${CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DIR}': set CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DIR to one "
                "(CI checks out Marcuss-ops/Chronon3d next to this repo).")
    endif()
    if(NOT EXISTS "${CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DIR}/include/chronon3d/graphics/field2d.hpp")
        message(FATAL_ERROR
                "ChrononTemplate needs chronon3d/graphics/field2d.hpp from a Chronon3D checkout at "
                "'${CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DIR}'.")
    endif()
    # GLM comes from the system first (CI: libglm-dev); the Chronon3D vcpkg tree
    # is the fallback so a checkout without system headers still configures.
    find_path(CHRONONTEMPLATE_GLM_DIR glm/glm.hpp
              HINTS "${CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DIR}/vcpkg_installed/linux-fast-dev/x64-linux/include")
    if(NOT CHRONONTEMPLATE_GLM_DIR)
        message(FATAL_ERROR
                "ChrononTemplate needs glm/glm.hpp (CI installs libglm-dev): no system GLM found "
                "and no vendored copy under '${CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DIR}/vcpkg_installed'.")
    endif()
    # magic_enum layout: upstream and vcpkg use `magic_enum/magic_enum.hpp`, but the
    # Ubuntu package (`libmagicenum-dev`) ships a flat `magic_enum.hpp`. Prefer the
    # real layout; otherwise generate a one-line compat header so Chronon3D's
    # `core/enum_utils.hpp` keeps compiling without a vendored third-party copy.
    find_path(CHRONONTEMPLATE_MAGIC_ENUM_DIR magic_enum/magic_enum.hpp
              HINTS "${CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DIR}/vcpkg_installed/linux-fast-dev/x64-linux/include")
    find_path(CHRONONTEMPLATE_MAGIC_ENUM_FLAT_DIR magic_enum.hpp)
    if(CHRONONTEMPLATE_MAGIC_ENUM_DIR)
        set(CHRONONTEMPLATE_MAGIC_ENUM_INCLUDE_DIR "${CHRONONTEMPLATE_MAGIC_ENUM_DIR}")
        message(STATUS "ChrononTemplate: using magic_enum layout at ${CHRONONTEMPLATE_MAGIC_ENUM_INCLUDE_DIR}")
    elseif(CHRONONTEMPLATE_MAGIC_ENUM_FLAT_DIR)
        file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/chronontemplate_compat/magic_enum")
        file(WRITE "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/chronontemplate_compat/magic_enum/magic_enum.hpp"
            "// Generated by ChrononTemplate: Ubuntu ships magic_enum flat, Chronon3D\n"
            "// includes the upstream magic_enum/magic_enum.hpp layout.\n"
            "#pragma once\n"
            "#include <magic_enum.hpp>\n")
        set(CHRONONTEMPLATE_MAGIC_ENUM_INCLUDE_DIR "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/chronontemplate_compat")
        message(STATUS "ChrononTemplate: bridging flat magic_enum.hpp via generated compat header")
    else()
        message(FATAL_ERROR
                "ChrononTemplate needs magic_enum (CI installs libmagicenum-dev): neither "
                "magic_enum/magic_enum.hpp nor a flat magic_enum.hpp was found.")
    endif()
    # stb layout, same story: vcpkg ships a flat `stb_image_write.h`, Ubuntu ships
    # `stb/stb_image_write.h`, and the camera tool includes the flat path.
    find_path(CHRONONTEMPLATE_STB_FLAT_DIR stb_image_write.h
              HINTS "${CHRONONTEMPLATE_CHRONON3D_DIR}/vcpkg_installed/linux-video-fast-dev/x64-linux/include")

    // Emit the WebPageV2Pack plans: three recipes · two themes, render-safe.
    // Rotation is authored in radians (the V1 degree bug killed video exports).
    #include "chronontemplate/web/WebPageV2Pack.hpp"
    
    #include <filesystem>
    #include <fstream>
    #include <iostream>
    #include <stdexcept>
    #include <string>
    
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    
    namespace {
    
        chronontemplate::web::WebPageV2Spec specFor(
                chronontemplate::web::WebPageV2Theme theme,
                chronontemplate::web::WebPageV2Recipe recipe) {
            using namespace chronontemplate::web;
            WebPageV2Spec spec;
            spec.theme = theme;
            spec.recipe = recipe;
            spec.siteName = "CHRONON NEWS";
            spec.navLinks = {"NBA", "Football", "Business", "Culture"};
            spec.kicker = "NBA TRADE DESK";
            spec.headlineLineOne = "Sources: Kuminga camp";
            spec.headlineLineTwo = "pushing for Warriors exit";
            spec.byline = "ANTHONY SLATER";
            spec.dateline = "Jan 15, 2026 · San Francisco";
            spec.meta = "JAN 15, 2026 · 08:58 PM";
            spec.leadLine = "Eligible to be moved for the first time this summer.";
            spec.bodyLines = {
                "The fifth-year forward demanded a trade away",
                "from the Warriors, league sources said, ending",
                "weeks of tension over his rotation spot.",
                "The contract he signed restricts any deal until",
                "the trade window opens in the first week of",
                "February, when talks are expected to resume",
                "quickly once front offices can negotiate again.",
                "Golden State has weighed staged return plans,",
                "including minutes charts and practice reps.",
                "His camp believes a fresh start lifts both sides.",
            };
            spec.pickTitles = {"Trade buzz: moves that could",
                               "land before the February window",
                               "How the deadline reshapes the West"};
            spec.importantPhrase = "THE FEBRUARY DEADLINE";
            spec.contextPhrases = {
                "Executives around the league expect the",
                "conversation to resume before the window opens,",
                "sources added, and the rotation spot has not",
                "really returned since the difficult stretch.",
                "Golden State has weighed staged return plans,",
                "with minutes charts drafted for each option.",
            };
            return spec;
        }
    
    }// namespace
    
    int main(int argc, char** argv) try {
        if (argc != 2) throw std::runtime_error("usage: emit_web_page_v2 <out-dir>");
        const fs::path outDir = fs::absolute(argv[1]);
        fs::create_directories(outDir);
    
        using namespace chronontemplate::web;
        int written = 0;
        for (int themeIndex = 0; themeIndex <= 1; ++themeIndex) {
            const WebPageV2Theme theme = themeIndex == 0 ? WebPageV2Theme::Light : WebPageV2Theme::Dark;
            for (int recipeIndex = 0; recipeIndex <= 2; ++recipeIndex) {
                const WebPageV2Recipe recipe = static_cast<WebPageV2Recipe>(recipeIndex);
                const auto variant = specFor(theme, recipe);
                const auto plan = buildWebPageV2Plan(variant);
                const fs::path out = outDir / (variant.planName() + ".plan.json");
                std::ofstream file(out);
                if (!file) throw std::runtime_error("cannot write plan: " + out.string());
                file << plan.dump(2) << '\n';
                std::cout << "Wrote " << out << '\n';
                ++written;
            }
        }
        std::cout << written << " native V2 plans (3 recipes x 2 themes, radians-safe)\n";
        return 0;
    } catch (const std::exception& error) {
        std::cerr << error.what() << '\n';
        return 1;
    }
        const char* name(WebPageV2Theme theme) {
            return theme == WebPageV2Theme::Light ? "light" : "dark";
        }
    
        const char* name(WebPageV2Recipe recipe) {
            switch (recipe) {
                case WebPageV2Recipe::Complete: return "complete";
                case WebPageV2Recipe::Highlight3D: return "highlight3d";
                case WebPageV2Recipe::LongPhraseBlurred: return "longphraseblurred";
            }
            return "unknown";
        }
    
        WebPageV2Palette paletteFor(WebPageV2Theme theme) {
            if (theme == WebPageV2Theme::Light) {
                return {.paper = "#FAF9F6", .nav = "#FFFFFF", .ink = "#191D23", .muted = "#6E747C",
                        .accent = "#C8392B", .link = "#1A56DB", .rule = "#E7E4DC", .panel = "#F2F0EA",
                        .panelLine = "#D9D7D0", .highlight = "#FFE45C", .body = "#3E434B"};
            }
            return {.paper = "#0E1116", .nav = "#151A21", .ink = "#F4F1E9", .muted = "#9AA3AE",
                    .accent = "#E8604C", .link = "#6FB7FF", .rule = "#222931", .panel = "#161C24",
                    .panelLine = "#272F3A", .highlight = "#E8604C", .body = "#C2C8D1"};
        }
    
        void WebPageV2Spec::validate() const {
            const bool longBlurred = recipe == WebPageV2Recipe::LongPhraseBlurred;
            if (siteName.empty()) fail("siteName is required");
            if (siteName.size() > 24) fail("siteName is too long (<= 24 chars)");
            if (navLinks.size() > 5) fail("at most five nav links");
            for (const std::string& link : navLinks) {
                if (link.empty() || link.size() > 16) fail("nav links must be 1..16 chars");
            }
            if (!longBlurred) {
                if (headlineLineOne.empty()) fail("headlineLineOne is required");
                if (headlineLineOne.size() > 44) fail("headlineLineOne is too long (<= 44 chars)");
                if (headlineLineTwo.size() > 44) fail("headlineLineTwo is too long (<= 44 chars)");
                if (kicker.empty()) fail("kicker is required");
                if (bodyLines.empty()) fail("bodyLines is required for the article body");
                if (bodyLines.size() > 12) fail("at most twelve body lines");
                if (pickTitles.size() > 3) fail("at most three sidebar picks");
            } else {
                if (importantPhrase.empty()) fail("importantPhrase is required");
                if (importantPhrase.size() > 44) fail("importantPhrase is too long (<= 44 chars)");
                if (contextPhrases.size() < 2) fail("at least two contextPhrases are required");
                if (contextPhrases.size() > 6) fail("at most six contextPhrases");
            }
            for (const std::vector<std::string>* fields : {&bodyLines, &pickTitles, &contextPhrases}) {
                for (const std::string& line : *fields) {
                    if (line.empty() || line.size() > 72) fail("rendered lines must be 1..72 chars");
                }
            }
            if (!leadLine.empty() && leadLine.size() > 72) fail("leadLine is too long (<= 72 chars)");
            for (const std::string* text : {&byline, &dateline, &meta, &actionLabel,
                                            &searchHint, &importantPhrase, &leadLine}) {

            }
