    /// Distanza camera che mappa 1 unita' = 1 px: il piano a z=0 riempie il canvas.
    /// Con fov verticale 50deg: (1080/2) / tan(25deg) = 1158.06.
    inline constexpr float kCameraBaseDistance = 1158.06f;
    
    /// Static camera: 1 unita' = 1 px. Con fov verticale 50deg la distanza che
    /// mappa 1080 unita' su 1080px e' 540/tan(25deg) = 1158.06 = kCameraBaseDistance
    /// (verificato con render di calibrazione: rettangoli a x 200/900/1600 tornano
    /// al px con -1158.06; la vecchia -1320 con yaw 0.5deg scalava tutto di 0.877
    /// verso il centro e traslava i bordi).
    inline Json staticCamera() {
        return Json{{"type", "perspective"},
                    {"position", Json::array({0.f, 0.f, -kCameraBaseDistance})},
                    {"rotation_deg", Json::array({0.f, 0.f, 0.f})},
                    {"fov_deg", 50.f}, {"near", 1.f}, {"far", 10000.f}, {"zoom", 1.f},
                    {"sensor_width_mm", 36.f}, {"lens_shift", Json::array({0.f, 0.f})}};
    }
    
    /// Camera samples per-frame: asse centrale e push molto leggero, senza yaw,
    /// roll, tilt o oscillazioni. Il push e' uno zoom ottico minimo, quindi non
    /// sposta gli elementi rispetto al centro del frame.
    inline Json cameraSamples(int duration) {
        Json samples = Json::array();
        for (int frame = 0; frame < duration; ++frame) {
            const float progress = duration > 1 ? float(frame) / float(duration - 1) : 1.f;
            const float zoom = 1.f + 0.035f * progress;
            Json camera = {
                {"type", "perspective"},
                {"position", Json::array({0.f, 0.f, -kCameraBaseDistance})},
                {"rotation_deg", Json::array({0.f, 0.f, 0.f})},
                {"fov_deg", 50.f}, {"near", 100.f}, {"far", 10000.f}, {"zoom", zoom},
                {"sensor_width_mm", 36.f},
                {"lens_shift", Json::array({0.f, 0.f})},
                {"dof", Json{{"enabled", false}, {"focus_distance", kCameraBaseDistance},
                             {"aperture", 0.f}, {"max_blur", 0.f}}}};
            samples.push_back(Json{{"frame", frame}, {"camera", std::move(camera)}});
        }
        return samples;
    }
    
    /// Port of Shot.camera()/apply_camera() camera inputs. The Python authoring
    /// data is a linear (zoom, center-x, center-y) move; keep the camera axis
    /// aligned to the pixel-authored layer plane instead of applying a shared
    /// dolly and yaw to every shot.
    inline Json cameraSamples(int duration, double zoomFrom, double cxFrom, double cyFrom,
                              double zoomTo, double cxTo, double cyTo) {
        Json samples = Json::array();
        for (int frame = 0; frame < duration; ++frame) {
            const double t = duration > 1 ? double(frame) / double(duration - 1) : 1.0;
            const double zoom = zoomFrom + (zoomTo - zoomFrom) * t;
            const double cx = cxFrom + (cxTo - cxFrom) * t;
            const double cy = cyFrom + (cyTo - cyFrom) * t;
            Json camera = {
                {"type", "perspective"},
                {"position", Json::array({(cx - 0.5) * kW, (0.5 - cy) * kH,
                                          -kCameraBaseDistance})},
                {"rotation_deg", Json::array({0.f, 0.f, 0.f})},
                {"fov_deg", 50.f}, {"near", 100.f}, {"far", 10000.f}, {"zoom", zoom},
        layer["animation"] = Json{{"tracks", std::move(kept)}};
    }
    
    /// Envelope `chronon.render-plan.v3` completa della composizione.
    ///
    /// Con una camera prospettica il renderer fa depth test: layer complanari
    /// si contengono a vicenda. Ogni layer riceve uno z leggermente piu'
    /// vicino alla camera del precedente (vedi kLayerDepthStep), cosi' il
    /// renderer conserva l'ordine autoriale del builder.
    inline Json renderPlan(const std::string& jobId, int duration, const Json& layers,
                           const Json& cameraSamplesJson) {
        // The current RenderPlan contract applies the plan camera directly. The
        // old writer baked a Python crop affine into layer tracks as well, which
        // double-transformed every shot after the camera pass changed. Keep one
        // transform authority: the camera stays static and the layers keep only
        // their authored tracks (marker sweeps, pops, etc.).
        (void)cameraSamplesJson;
        Json stack = Json::array();
        for (const Json& authored : layers) {
            Json layer = authored;
            const bool hasMarkerCore = layer.contains("_native_marker_core_alpha");
            const double coreAlpha = hasMarkerCore ? layer["_native_marker_core_alpha"].get<double>() : 1.0;
            layer.erase("_native_marker_core_alpha");
            layer.erase("_v4_highlight");
            // Painter order: i layer successivi siedono piu' vicini alla camera
            // (camera a z=-1158: z piu' negativo = piu' vicino). Il core del
            // marker segue subito il bordo grezzo cosi' resta sopra di esso e
            // sotto i glifi del testo.
            auto pushWithDepth = [&](Json l) {
                if (l.contains("position") && l["position"].is_array() &&
                    l["position"].size() >= 3)
                    l["position"][2] = -kLayerDepthStep * float(stack.size());
                stack.push_back(std::move(l));
            };
            pushWithDepth(layer);
            if (hasMarkerCore) {
                // Banda core del pennarello (Python: rect denso al 56% altezza):
                // stesso centro, stesse track di sweep del bordo, un layer solo.
                Json core = authored;
                core.erase("_native_marker_core_alpha");
                core.erase("_v4_highlight");
                const std::string id = authored.value("id", std::string{});
                const float w = authored["size"][0].get<float>();
                const float h = authored["size"][1].get<float>();
                core["id"] = id + "_core";
                core["size"] = Json::array({w, h * 0.56f});
                core["shape"] = {{"type", "rect"}, {"fill", authored["shape"]["fill"]}};
                if (core["shape"]["fill"].is_array()) core["shape"]["fill"][3] = coreAlpha;
                pushWithDepth(std::move(core));
            }
        }
        return {{"schema", "chronon.render-plan.v3"}, {"version", 3}, {"job_id", jobId},
                {"canvas", {{"width", kW}, {"height", kH}, {"fps_num", kFps}, {"fps_den", 1},
                            {"duration_frames", duration}}},
                {"layers", std::move(stack)}, {"camera", staticCamera()}};
    }

    const json* layerById(const json& plan, const std::string& id) {
        for (const auto& layer : plan.at("layers"))
            if (layer.value("id", std::string{}) == id) return &layer;
        return nullptr;
    }
    
    /// Keyframe value of a track; -1 when the layer has no such track.
    float keyValue(const json& layer, const std::string& property, bool first) {
        if (!layer.contains("animation")) return -1.f;
        for (const auto& track : layer.at("animation").at("tracks")) {
            if (track.value("property", std::string{}) != property) continue;
            const auto& keys = track.at("keyframes");
            return (first ? keys.front() : keys.back()).at("value").get<float>();
        }
        return -1.f;
    }
    
    /// Authored left edge in canvas px. Images are centre-relative; shapes are
    /// absolute top-down in this pack.
    float leftEdge(const json& layer) {
        const float centre = layer.at("position")[0].get<float>();
        return (layer.value("type", "") == "shape" ? centre : centre + 960.f) -
               layer.at("size")[0].get<float>() * 0.5f;
    }
    
    void checksEnvelope(const json& plan, const std::string& jobId, int duration) {
        check(plan.at("schema") == "chronon.render-plan.v3" && plan.at("version") == 3,
              "the plan is render-plan V3");
        check(plan.at("job_id") == jobId, "the job id follows the recipe identity");
        const auto& canvas = plan.at("canvas");
        check(canvas.at("width") == 1920 && canvas.at("height") == 1080,
              "the canvas is 1920x1080");
        check(canvas.at("fps_num") == 30 && canvas.at("fps_den") == 1,
              "the canvas is 30 fps");
        check(canvas.at("duration_frames") == duration,
              "the canvas carries the authored duration");
        check(plan.at("output").at("format") == "mp4" &&
                  plan.at("output").at("codec") == "h264",
              "the output is H.264 mp4");
        check(plan.contains("camera") && plan.at("camera").at("type") == "perspective",
              "the plan declares a perspective camera");
        check(!plan.contains("camera_samples"),
              "the plan does not carry obsolete camera samples");
    }
    
    void checksLayers(const json& plan) {
        std::set<std::string> ids;
        for (const auto& layer : plan.at("layers")) {
            check(ids.insert(layer.at("id").get<std::string>()).second,
                  "layer ids are unique inside the plan");
            check(layer.at("position").is_array() && layer.at("position").size() >= 2,
                  "every layer has a position");
            if (layer.at("type") == "image") {
                check(layer.contains("asset") && !layer.at("asset").get<std::string>().empty(),
                      "an image layer names its content asset");
            }
        }
        check(plan.at("layers").size() >= 2, "the recipe composes a real scene");
    }

    inline Json cameraSamples(int duration) {
        Json samples = Json::array();
        for (int frame = 0; frame < duration; ++frame) {
            const float progress = duration > 1 ? float(frame) / float(duration - 1) : 1.f;
            const float zoom = 1.f + 0.035f * progress;
            Json camera = {
                {"type", "perspective"},
                {"position", Json::array({0.f, 0.f, -kCameraBaseDistance})},
                {"rotation_deg", Json::array({0.f, 0.f, 0.f})},
                {"fov_deg", 50.f}, {"near", 100.f}, {"far", 10000.f}, {"zoom", zoom},

    /// Con una camera prospettica il renderer fa depth test: layer complanari
    /// si contengono a vicenda. Ogni layer riceve uno z leggermente piu'
    /// vicino alla camera del precedente (vedi kLayerDepthStep), cosi' il
    /// renderer conserva l'ordine autoriale del builder.
    inline Json renderPlan(const std::string& jobId, int duration, const Json& layers,
                           const Json& cameraSamplesJson) {
        // The current RenderPlan contract applies the plan camera directly. The
        // old writer baked a Python crop affine into layer tracks as well, which
        // double-transformed every shot after the camera pass changed. Keep one
        // transform authority: the camera stays static and the layers keep only
        // their authored tracks (marker sweeps, pops, etc.).
        (void)cameraSamplesJson;
        Json stack = Json::array();
        for (const Json& authored : layers) {
            Json layer = authored;
            const bool hasMarkerCore = layer.contains("_native_marker_core_alpha");
            const double coreAlpha = hasMarkerCore ? layer["_native_marker_core_alpha"].get<double>() : 1.0;
            layer.erase("_native_marker_core_alpha");
            layer.erase("_v4_highlight");
            // Painter order: i layer successivi siedono piu' vicini alla camera
            // (camera a z=-1158: z piu' negativo = piu' vicino). Il core del
            // marker segue subito il bordo grezzo cosi' resta sopra di esso e
            // sotto i glifi del testo.
            auto pushWithDepth = [&](Json l) {
                if (l.contains("position") && l["position"].is_array() &&
                    l["position"].size() >= 3)
                    l["position"][2] = -kLayerDepthStep * float(stack.size());
                stack.push_back(std::move(l));
            };
            pushWithDepth(layer);
            if (hasMarkerCore) {
                // Banda core del pennarello (Python: rect denso al 56% altezza):
                // stesso centro, stesse track di sweep del bordo, un layer solo.
                Json core = authored;
                core.erase("_native_marker_core_alpha");
                core.erase("_v4_highlight");
                const std::string id = authored.value("id", std::string{});
                const float w = authored["size"][0].get<float>();
                const float h = authored["size"][1].get<float>();
                core["id"] = id + "_core";
                core["size"] = Json::array({w, h * 0.56f});
                core["shape"] = {{"type", "rect"}, {"fill", authored["shape"]["fill"]}};
                if (core["shape"]["fill"].is_array()) core["shape"]["fill"][3] = coreAlpha;
                pushWithDepth(std::move(core));
            }
        }
        return {{"schema", "chronon.render-plan.v3"}, {"version", 3}, {"job_id", jobId},
                {"canvas", {{"width", kW}, {"height", kH}, {"fps_num", kFps}, {"fps_den", 1},
                            {"duration_frames", duration}}},
                {"layers", std::move(stack)}, {"camera", staticCamera()}};
    }

    /// #RRGGBB -> [r,g,b,a] in 0..1 (stessa codifica di Material::rgba).
    inline Json rgba(const std::string& hex, float alpha = 1.f) {
        const auto value = std::stoul(hex.substr(1), nullptr, 16);
        return Json::array({((value >> 16) & 255) / 255.0, ((value >> 8) & 255) / 255.0,
                            (value & 255) / 255.0, static_cast<double>(alpha)});
    }

    /// `position` e' il centro del layer. Lo z e' assegnato da renderPlan.

        // Same contract as WebPageV2Pack: position is the
        // layer center in top-left-down px for X and bottom-left-up px for Y.
        return Json::array({topDownCenterX, float(kH) - topDownCenterY, z});

        Json samples = Json::array();

            const double t = duration > 1 ? double(frame) / double(duration - 1) : 1.0;
            const double zoom = zoomFrom + (zoomTo - zoomFrom) * t;

            const double cy = cyFrom + (cyTo - cyFrom) * t;
            Json camera = {
                {"type", "perspective"},
                {"position", Json::array({(cx - 0.5) * kW, (0.5 - cy) * kH,
                                          -kCameraBaseDistance})},
                {"rotation_deg", Json::array({0.f, 0.f, 0.f})},
                {"fov_deg", 50.f}, {"near", 100.f}, {"far", 10000.f}, {"zoom", zoom},
                {"sensor_width_mm", 36.f}, {"lens_shift", Json::array({0.f, 0.f})},
                {"dof", Json{{"enabled", false}, {"focus_distance", kCameraBaseDistance},
                             {"aperture", 0.f}, {"max_blur", 0.f}}}};
            samples.push_back(Json{{"frame", frame}, {"camera", std::move(camera)}});
        }
        return samples;
    }

    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    
    int main(int argc, char** argv) try {
        if (argc != 2) {
            throw std::runtime_error(
                "usage: chronontemplate_emit_web_paper_reference <output-dir>");
        }
        const fs::path out = fs::absolute(argv[1]);
        fs::create_directories(out);
        for (const auto recipe : chronontemplate::web::allPaperReferenceRecipes()) {
            chronontemplate::web::PaperReferenceSpec spec;
            spec.recipe = recipe;
            const auto plan = chronontemplate::web::buildPaperReferencePlan(spec);
            const fs::path path = out / (spec.planName() + ".plan.json");
            std::ofstream file(path);
            if (!file) throw std::runtime_error("cannot write " + path.string());
            file << plan.dump(2) << '\n';
            std::cout << path.string() << '\n';
        }
        return 0;
    } catch (const std::exception& error) {
        std::cerr << error.what() << '\n';
        return 1;
    }

    Json cameraAt(float focus, float fStop = 5.6f, bool dof = true, float x = 0.f,
                  float y = 0.f, float z = kCameraZ, float roll = 0.f,
                  float zoom = 1.f) {
        Json camera = {{"type", "perspective"},
                       {"position", Json::array({x, y, z})},
                       {"rotation_deg", Json::array({0.f, 0.f, roll})},
                       {"fov_deg", 50.f}, {"near", 1.f}, {"far", 10000.f},
                       {"zoom", zoom}, {"sensor_width_mm", 36.f},
                       {"lens_shift", Json::array({0.f, 0.f})},
                       {"dof", {{"enabled", dof}, {"focus_distance", focus},
                                {"max_blur", 26.f}, {"highlight_gain", 0.35f}}}};
        if (dof) camera["f_stop"] = fStop;
        return camera;
    }
    
    Json driftSamples(int duration, float amountX, float amountY, float amountRoll,
                      bool dof = false, float focus = 1158.06f, float fStop = 8.f) {
        Json samples = Json::array();
        for (int frame = 0; frame < duration; ++frame) {
            const float t = duration > 1 ? static_cast<float>(frame) /
                                          static_cast<float>(duration - 1) : 1.f;
            const float x = (t - 0.5f) * 2.f * amountX;
            const float y = std::sin(t * 6.2831853f) * amountY;
            const float roll = std::sin(t * 6.2831853f + 0.8f) * amountRoll;
            samples.push_back(Json{{"frame", frame},
                                   {"camera", cameraAt(focus, fStop, dof, x, y,
                                                       kCameraZ, roll, 1.f)}});
        }
        return samples;
    }

    /// Espressa come offset wire (origine centro, Y up) sommato alla base del
    /// layer: off = base*(z-1) + (tx, ty), con tx = (960-x0)*z - 960 e
    /// ty = y0*z - 540*(z-1)  [x0,y0 = crop top-left in px]. Il renderer somma le
    /// track position_* alla base, quindi questi offset bucati nelle track
    /// riproducono il crop 1:1 (verificato: carta ferma a frame 0, crop a 89).
    struct CamAffine { double z{1.0}, tx{0.0}, ty{0.0}; };
    
    inline std::vector<CamAffine> cameraAffines(const Json& samples, int duration) {
        std::vector<CamAffine> out(static_cast<std::size_t>(std::max(1, duration)));
        if (!samples.is_array()) return out;
        for (const Json& sample : samples) {
            if (!sample.is_object() || !sample.contains("camera") || !sample.contains("frame"))
                continue;
            const int frame = int(std::lround(sample.at("frame").get<double>()));
            if (frame < 0 || frame >= int(out.size())) continue;
            const Json& cam = sample.at("camera");
            const double zoom = std::max(1e-6, cam.value("zoom", 1.0));
            double cx = 0.5, cy = 0.5;
            if (cam.contains("position") && cam["position"].is_array() && cam["position"].size() >= 2) {
                cx = cam["position"][0].get<double>() / double(kW) + 0.5;
                cy = 0.5 - cam["position"][1].get<double>() / double(kH);
            }
            const double cw = double(kW) / zoom;
            const double ch = double(kH) / zoom;
            const double x0 = std::clamp(cx * double(kW) - cw * 0.5, 0.0, std::max(0.0, double(kW) - cw));
            const double y0 = std::clamp(cy * double(kH) - ch * 0.5, 0.0, std::max(0.0, double(kH) - ch));
            out[static_cast<std::size_t>(frame)] =
                CamAffine{zoom, (double(kW) * 0.5 - x0) * zoom - double(kW) * 0.5,
                           y0 * zoom - double(kH) * 0.5 * (zoom - 1.0)};
        }
        return out;
    }
    
    /// Stesse curve di easing del renderer (glm: cubicEase*/backEaseOut).
    inline double easingEval(const std::string& name, double u) {
        u = std::clamp(u, 0.0, 1.0);
        if (name == "in_out_cubic") return u < 0.5 ? 4.0 * u * u * u
                                                   : 1.0 - std::pow(-2.0 * u + 2.0, 3.0) / 2.0;
        if (name == "out_cubic") { const double f = u - 1.0; return f * f * f + 1.0; }
        if (name == "in_cubic") return u * u * u;
        if (name == "out_back") { const double c1 = 1.70158, n = u - 1.0;
                                   return 1.0 + n * n * ((c1 + 1.0) * n + c1); }
        return u; // linear
    }

    /// Poligono arbitrario in coordinate autore (top-left-down). Il bbox diventa

    /// (`Canvas.poly`) prima del blur di placca.
    inline Json poly(const std::string& id, const std::vector<std::pair<float, float>>& pts,
                     const std::string& hex, float alpha, int duration = 90, float blur = 0.f) {
        if (pts.size() < 3) throw std::invalid_argument("poly needs at least 3 points");
        float minx = pts[0].first, maxx = minx, miny = pts[0].second, maxy = miny;
        for (const auto& p : pts) {
            minx = std::min(minx, p.first);  maxx = std::max(maxx, p.first);

    /// Baked linear blur animator (il decoder richiede keyframe campionati).
    inline Json blurAnimator(const std::string& id, float blur, int duration) {
        Json selector = Json::object();
        selector["id"] = id + "_sel";
        selector["unit"] = "character";
        selector["shape"] = "square";
        selector["order"] = "forward";
        selector["combine"] = "replace";
        selector["exclude_spaces"] = false;
        selector["start"] = Json{{"keyframes", Json::array({Json{{"frame", 0}, {"value", 0.0}}})},

        selector["end"] = Json{{"keyframes", Json::array({Json{{"frame", 0}, {"value", 100.0}}})},
                               {"easing", "linear"}};
        Json property = Json::object();
        property["property"] = "blur";
        property["easing"] = "linear";
        property["keyframes"] = Json::array({Json{{"frame", 0}, {"value", blur}},
                                             Json{{"frame", duration - 1}, {"value", blur}}});
        Json animator = Json::object();
        animator["id"] = id + "_blur";
        animator["selectors"] = Json::array({selector});
        animator["properties"] = Json::array({property});
        return animator;
    }
    
    namespace modules {
    inline Json renderPlan(const std::string& jobId, int duration, const Json& layers,
                           const Json& cameraSamplesJson) {
        // The current RenderPlan contract applies the plan camera directly. The
        // old writer baked a Python crop affine into layer tracks as well, which
        // double-transformed every shot after the camera pass changed. Keep one
        // transform authority: the camera stays static and the layers keep only
        // their authored tracks (marker sweeps, pops, etc.).
        (void)cameraSamplesJson;
        Json stack = Json::array();
        for (const Json& authored : layers) {
            Json layer = authored;
            const bool hasMarkerCore = layer.contains("_native_marker_core_alpha");
            const double coreAlpha = hasMarkerCore ? layer["_native_marker_core_alpha"].get<double>() : 1.0;
            layer.erase("_native_marker_core_alpha");
            layer.erase("_v4_highlight");
            // Painter order: i layer successivi siedono piu' vicini alla camera
            // (camera a z=-1158: z piu' negativo = piu' vicino). Il core del
            // marker segue subito il bordo grezzo cosi' resta sopra di esso e
            // sotto i glifi del testo.
            auto pushWithDepth = [&](Json l) {
                if (l.contains("position") && l["position"].is_array() &&
                    l["position"].size() >= 3)
                    l["position"][2] = -kLayerDepthStep * float(stack.size());
                stack.push_back(std::move(l));
            };
            pushWithDepth(layer);
            if (hasMarkerCore) {
                // Banda core del pennarello (Python: rect denso al 56% altezza):
                // stesso centro, stesse track di sweep del bordo, un layer solo.
                Json core = authored;
                core.erase("_native_marker_core_alpha");
                core.erase("_v4_highlight");
                const std::string id = authored.value("id", std::string{});
                const float w = authored["size"][0].get<float>();
                const float h = authored["size"][1].get<float>();
                core["id"] = id + "_core";
                core["size"] = Json::array({w, h * 0.56f});
                core["shape"] = {{"type", "rect"}, {"fill", authored["shape"]["fill"]}};
                if (core["shape"]["fill"].is_array()) core["shape"]["fill"][3] = coreAlpha;
                pushWithDepth(std::move(core));
            }
        }
        return {{"schema", "chronon.render-plan.v3"}, {"version", 3}, {"job_id", jobId},
                {"canvas", {{"width", kW}, {"height", kH}, {"fps_num", kFps}, {"fps_den", 1},
                            {"duration_frames", duration}}},
                {"layers", std::move(stack)}, {"camera", staticCamera()}};
    }

    /// #RRGGBB -> [r,g,b,a] in 0..1 (stessa codifica di Material::rgba).
    inline Json rgba(const std::string& hex, float alpha = 1.f) {
        const auto value = std::stoul(hex.substr(1), nullptr, 16);
        return Json::array({((value >> 16) & 255) / 255.0, ((value >> 8) & 255) / 255.0,
                            (value & 255) / 255.0, static_cast<double>(alpha)});
    }

    /// pixel-truth raw: wire [-760,-340] centra un box su (200,880) px).
    /// `position` e' il centro del layer. Lo z e' assegnato da renderPlan.
    inline Json wirePos(float topDownCenterX, float topDownCenterY, float z = 0.f) {
        // Same contract as WebPageV2Pack: position is the
        // layer center in top-left-down px for X and bottom-left-up px for Y.
        return Json::array({topDownCenterX, float(kH) - topDownCenterY, z});
    }

    // Emit the five native paper-reference plans as RenderPlan V3 documents.
    #include "chronontemplate/web/WebPaperReferencePack.hpp"
    
    #include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
    
    #include <filesystem>
    #include <fstream>
    #include <iostream>
    #include <stdexcept>
    #include <string>
    
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    
    int main(int argc, char** argv) try {
        if (argc != 2) {
            throw std::runtime_error(
                "usage: chronontemplate_emit_web_paper_reference <output-dir>");
        }
        const fs::path out = fs::absolute(argv[1]);
        fs::create_directories(out);
        for (const auto recipe : chronontemplate::web::allPaperReferenceRecipes()) {
            chronontemplate::web::PaperReferenceSpec spec;
            spec.recipe = recipe;
            const auto plan = chronontemplate::web::buildPaperReferencePlan(spec);
            const fs::path path = out / (spec.planName() + ".plan.json");
            std::ofstream file(path);
            if (!file) throw std::runtime_error("cannot write " + path.string());
            file << plan.dump(2) << '\n';
            std::cout << path.string() << '\n';
        }
        return 0;
    } catch (const std::exception& error) {
        std::cerr << error.what() << '\n';
        return 1;
    }

    // The paper pages, torn strip and archive photograph are static content assets;

    // RenderPlan V3 layers. A flat lighting rig keeps raster and shape albedo at

    #include <array>

    namespace chronontemplate::web {

    using namespace shot;
    
    constexpr const char* kAssetDir = "assets/web_reference_rebuild_20261114/";
    constexpr const char* kInk = "#171614";
    constexpr const char* kPaper = "#D9D8D3";

    constexpr const char* kCharcoal = "#141414";

    // Resolved against the ChrononTemplate assets root, like the paper assets.

    constexpr const char* kFontPlayfairBold = "assets/fonts/PlayfairDisplay-Bold.ttf";
    
    [[noreturn]] void fail(const std::string& message) {
        throw std::invalid_argument("PaperReferenceSpec: " + message);
    }
    
    std::string asset(const char* name) {
        return std::string(kAssetDir) + name;
    }
    
    /// Two-key linear/eased channel, safe when the window starts at frame 0.
    Json twoKeyTrack(const std::string& property, float from, float to, int duration,
                     const std::string& easing) {
        return Json{{"property", property}, {"easing", easing},
                    {"keyframes", Json::array({
                        Json{{"frame", 0}, {"value", from}},
                        Json{{"frame", std::max(1, duration - 1)}, {"value", to}}})}};
    }
    
    /// Fade in and hold; no duplicate frame-0 key when start is 0.
    Json fadeTrack(int duration, int start, int span, float peak = 1.f) {
        Json keys = Json::array();
        if (start > 0) keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", 0}, {"value", 0.0}});
        keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", start}, {"value", 0.0}});
        keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", start + span}, {"value", peak}});
        keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", std::max(1, duration - 1)}, {"value", peak}});
        return Json{{"property", "opacity"}, {"easing", "out_cubic"},
                    {"keyframes", std::move(keys)}};
    }
    
    Json moveTrack(const std::string& property, float from, float to, int duration,
                   int start, int span, const std::string& easing) {
        Json keys = Json::array();
        if (start > 0) keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", 0}, {"value", from}});
        keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", start}, {"value", from}});
        keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", start + span}, {"value", to}});
        keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", std::max(1, duration - 1)}, {"value", to}});
        return Json{{"property", property}, {"easing", easing},
                    {"keyframes", std::move(keys)}};
    }
    
    void tracks(Json& layer, Json value) {
        layer["animation"] = Json{{"tracks", std::move(value)}};
    }
    
    /// Shapes share the text layer's absolute top-down space. `rect`/`ellipse`
    /// already emit the absolute center X and a bottom-up Y through wirePos, so
    /// only Y needs converting. The old pass also removed the canvas centre from
    /// both axes; the renderer read that as absolute, parking shadows and
    /// watermark boxes in the top-left corner. Full-frame screen-space plates
    /// already sit at [0,0] and are left alone.
    Json shiftShape(Json layer) {
        if (layer.value("screen_space", false)) return layer;
        if (layer.contains("position") && layer["position"].is_array() &&
            layer["position"].size() >= 2) {
            layer["position"][1] = 1080.f - layer["position"][1].get<float>();
        }
        return layer;
    }
    
    Json panel(const std::string& id, float left, float top, float width, float height,
               const std::string& color, float alpha, int duration) {
        return shiftShape(rect(id, left, top, width, height, color, alpha, Json::array(),
                               duration));
    }
    
    /// Native path fill is not rasterized by the Vulkan plan executor; the
    /// referenced marker strokes are feathered textures, so the band is an image
    /// swept with scale_x/position_x exactly like the native marker primitive.
    Json marker(const std::string& id, const std::string& file, float left, float top,
                float width, float height, int begin, int span, int duration) {
        Json band = image(id, asset(file.c_str()), left, top, width, height, duration);
        tracks(band, sweepTracks(width, begin, span));
        // The marker image is composited over the sharp text plate on this backend.
        // Keep the band translucent so the ink stays readable while it sweeps.
        for (Json& track : band["animation"]["tracks"]) {
            if (track.value("property", std::string{}) != "opacity") continue;
            for (Json& key : track["keyframes"]) {
                key["value"] = key["value"].get<float>() * 0.38f;
            }
        }
        return band;
    }
    
    
    /// The 2.5D pose is baked into the page plate: image-layer rotation is not
    /// applied by the executor, while the transform still shows real perspective.
    Json paperPage(int duration) {
        Json page = image("la_times_page", asset("la_times_page_tilted.png"), 0, 0,
                          1920, 1080, duration);
        // The baked plate is already full-bleed (its quad clears all four frame
        // edges), so a 1.0->1.05 push keeps coverage and the whole headline.
        tracks(page, Json::array({
            twoKeyTrack("scale", 1.f, 1.05f, duration, "in_out_cubic"),
            twoKeyTrack("position_x", -6.f, 10.f, duration, "in_out_cubic"),
            twoKeyTrack("position_y", 4.f, -4.f, duration, "in_out_cubic")}));
        return page;
    }
    
    /// Lift the sharp text plate clear of the marker depth range. At 0.05 steps the
    /// Vulkan depth buffer resolves the 1 px marker/text contact unreliably.
    Json liftAbove(Json plan, const std::string& id, float z = -0.8f) {
        for (Json& layer : plan["layers"]) {
            if (layer.value("id", std::string{}) == id && layer.contains("position") &&
                layer["position"].is_array() && layer["position"].size() >= 3) {
                layer["position"][2] = z;
            }
        }
        return plan;
    }

        return renderPlan("web_ref_newspaper_tilt_v1", D, layers, staticCamera());
    }
    
    // ── 2. Torn paper strip ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Json buildTornStrip(int D) {
        Json layers = Json::array();
        Json bg = image("charcoal", asset("torn_bg.png"), 0, 0, 1920, 1080, D);
        tracks(bg, Json::array({
            twoKeyTrack("scale", 1.025f, 1.f, D, "in_out_cubic"),
            twoKeyTrack("position_y", 5.f, 0.f, D, "in_out_cubic")}));
        layers.push_back(std::move(bg));
    
        Json strip = image("torn_strip", asset("torn_strip_base.png"), 70, 320, 1800, 460, D);
        layers.push_back(std::move(strip));
    
        // The strip text starts at x=70+120 and is 1578 px wide at 62 px, so the
        // strip fills the frame like the macro reference instead of floating small.
        // This stroke is a texture: its edges undulate like a real marker line.
        layers.push_back(marker("strip_marker", "marker_strip.png", 190, 430, 1586, 78,
                                38, 62, D));
        Json strip_text = image("torn_strip_text", asset("torn_strip_text.png"), 70, 320,
                                1800, 460, D);
        layers.push_back(std::move(strip_text));
        return liftAbove(renderPlan("web_ref_torn_strip_v1", D, layers, staticCamera()),
                         "torn_strip_text");
    }
    
    // ── 3. Sharp evidence over a defocused newspaper ────────────────────────────
    Json buildBlurredEvidence(int D) {
        Json layers = Json::array();
        Json bg = image("blurred_newspaper", asset("evidence_bg.png"), 0, 0, 1920, 1080, D);
        tracks(bg, Json::array({
            twoKeyTrack("scale", 1.045f, 1.f, D, "in_out_cubic"),
            twoKeyTrack("position_y", 8.f, 0.f, D, "in_out_cubic")}));
        layers.push_back(std::move(bg));
    
        // No card, border or shadow: the sharp paragraph floats directly over the
        // defocused page, as in the supplied frame. Marker widths follow the text:
        // "whether a" at the end of line 4, full lines 5-6, "Arizona State" on 7.
        layers.push_back(marker("evidence_marker_3", "marker_evidence_3.png", 1209, 440,
                                251, 68, 42, 28, D));
        layers.push_back(marker("evidence_marker_4", "marker_evidence_4.png", 230, 515,
                                1400, 70, 54, 44, D));
        layers.push_back(marker("evidence_marker_5", "marker_evidence_5.png", 230, 595,
                                1300, 72, 66, 44, D));
        layers.push_back(marker("evidence_marker_6", "marker_evidence_6.png", 230, 675,
                                340, 72, 84, 26, D));
    
        Json text = image("evidence_text", asset("evidence_text.png"), 0, 0, 1920, 1080, D);
        layers.push_back(std::move(text));
    
        for (const Json& layer : sWatermark(D)) layers.push_back(layer);
        return liftAbove(renderPlan("web_ref_blurred_evidence_v1", D, layers, staticCamera()),
                         "evidence_text");
    }
    
    // ── 4. Archival collage with the Golden Gate photograph ─────────────────────
    Json buildBridgeCollage(int D) {
        Json layers = Json::array();
        // The two title lines are baked into the plate: the camera-path text and
        // image passes both offset these runs past the right edge, while a
        // full-frame plate keeps the authored left edge exactly.
        Json bg = image("collage_background", asset("collage_bg_titled.png"), 0, 0, 1920, 1080, D);
        tracks(bg, Json::array({
            twoKeyTrack("scale", 1.035f, 1.f, D, "in_out_cubic"),
            twoKeyTrack("position_y", 6.f, 0.f, D, "in_out_cubic")}));
        layers.push_back(std::move(bg));
    
        // Narrative continuity: the previous shot's defocused paragraph survives
        // at the left edge, behind the title and the photo.
        Json left = image("collage_left_text", asset("collage_left_text.png"), 0, 260,
                          620, 520, D);
        tracks(left, Json::array({fadeTrack(D, 4, 14)}));
        layers.push_back(std::move(left));
    
        const Json rise = moveTrack("position_y", 24.f, 0.f, D, 10, 28, "out_cubic");
        const Json reveal = fadeTrack(D, 8, 20);
    
        Json photo = image("golden_gate_photo", asset("bridge_bw.png"), 496, 328, 1024, 616, D);
        tracks(photo, Json::array({rise, reveal}));
        layers.push_back(std::move(photo));
    
        for (const Json& layer : sWatermark(D)) layers.push_back(layer);
        return renderPlan("web_ref_bridge_collage_v1", D, layers, staticCamera());
    }

    const char* paperReferenceName(PaperReferenceRecipe recipe) {
        switch (recipe) {
            case PaperReferenceRecipe::NewspaperTilt: return "web_ref_newspaper_tilt";
            case PaperReferenceRecipe::TornStrip: return "web_ref_torn_strip";
            case PaperReferenceRecipe::BlurredEvidence: return "web_ref_blurred_evidence";
            case PaperReferenceRecipe::BridgeCollage: return "web_ref_bridge_collage";
            case PaperReferenceRecipe::BookHighlight: return "web_ref_book_highlight";
        }
        return "unknown";
    }
    
    std::array<PaperReferenceRecipe, 5> allPaperReferenceRecipes() {
        return {PaperReferenceRecipe::NewspaperTilt, PaperReferenceRecipe::TornStrip,
                PaperReferenceRecipe::BlurredEvidence, PaperReferenceRecipe::BridgeCollage,
                PaperReferenceRecipe::BookHighlight};
    }
    
    void PaperReferenceSpec::validate() const {
        if (fps != 30) fail("fps must be 30");
        if (durationFrames < 30 || durationFrames > 300)
            fail("durationFrames must be in [30,300] (max 10 s at 30 fps)");
        if (outputName.find('\n') != std::string::npos)
            fail("outputName must be a single line");
    }
    
    std::string PaperReferenceSpec::planName() const {
        return std::string(paperReferenceName(recipe)) + "_v1";
    }
    
    std::string PaperReferenceSpec::outputStem() const {
        return outputName.empty() ? planName() + ".mp4" : outputName;
    }
    
    nlohmann::json buildPaperReferencePlan(const PaperReferenceSpec& spec) {
        spec.validate();
        const int duration = spec.durationFrames;
        Json plan;
        switch (spec.recipe) {
            case PaperReferenceRecipe::NewspaperTilt:
                plan = buildNewspaperTilt(duration);
                break;
            case PaperReferenceRecipe::TornStrip:
                plan = buildTornStrip(duration);
                break;
            case PaperReferenceRecipe::BlurredEvidence:
                plan = buildBlurredEvidence(duration);
                break;
            case PaperReferenceRecipe::BridgeCollage:
                plan = buildBridgeCollage(duration);
                break;
            case PaperReferenceRecipe::BookHighlight:
                plan = buildBookHighlight(duration);
                break;
        }
        // Image and shape albedo is lit by this rig. Without it the renderer's
        // default lighting multiplies paper and markers by roughly 0.48.
        plan["lighting_rig"] = Json{
            {"key_direction", Json::array({0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f})},
            {"key_intensity", 0.0f},
            {"key_color", Json::array({1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f})},
            {"ambient_intensity", 1.0f},
            {"ambient_color", Json::array({1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f})},
            {"rim_enabled", false},
            {"rim_intensity", 0.0f},
            {"rim_power", 1.0f},
            {"rim_color", Json::array({1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f})}};
        plan["job_id"] = spec.planName();
        plan["output"] = Json{{"path", spec.outputStem()}, {"format", "mp4"},
                              {"codec", "h264"}};
        return plan;
    }
    
    }  // namespace chronontemplate::web
    // ChrononTemplate — native rebuilds of five supplied web/paper reference frames.
    //
    // The five recipes are pure RenderPlan V3 compositions:
    //   * a LA Times page tilted in 2.5D on a dark desk,
    //   * a torn paper strip on charcoal with a progressive highlighter,
    //   * a sharp evidence paragraph over a heavily blurred newspaper,
    //   * an archival collage with a framed Golden Gate photograph,
    //   * a book page whose yellow highlighter fills left-to-right.
    //
    // The paper artwork is a raster content asset (the same pattern as the
    // existing newspaper family); every transform, marker sweep, shadow and
    // camera pose is authored here as native plan data. No browser or live DOM.
    #ifndef CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_PAPER_REFERENCE_PACK_HPP
    #define CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_PAPER_REFERENCE_PACK_HPP
    
    #include <array>
    #include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
    #include <string>
    
    namespace chronontemplate::web {
    
    enum class PaperReferenceRecipe : unsigned char {
        NewspaperTilt,     // LA Times page, perspective tilt, slow settle
        TornStrip,         // ragged paper strip, charcoal ground, yellow sweep
        BlurredEvidence,   // sharp paragraph over a defocused newspaper
        BridgeCollage,     // archival title + framed Golden Gate photograph
        BookHighlight      // book page, progressive multiple-blend highlighter
    };
    
    [[nodiscard]] const char* paperReferenceName(PaperReferenceRecipe recipe);
    [[nodiscard]] std::array<PaperReferenceRecipe, 5> allPaperReferenceRecipes();
    
    struct PaperReferenceSpec {
        PaperReferenceRecipe recipe{PaperReferenceRecipe::NewspaperTilt};
        int durationFrames{180};  // 6 s at 30 fps
        int fps{30};
        std::string outputName{};
    
        void validate() const;
        [[nodiscard]] std::string planName() const;
        [[nodiscard]] std::string outputStem() const;
    };
    
    /// Complete `chronon.render-plan.v3` document for one recipe.
    [[nodiscard]] nlohmann::json buildPaperReferencePlan(const PaperReferenceSpec& spec);
    
    }  // namespace chronontemplate::web
    
    #endif  // CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_PAPER_REFERENCE_PACK_HPP

    /// #RRGGBB -> [r,g,b,a] in 0..1 (stessa codifica di Material::rgba).
    inline Json rgba(const std::string& hex, float alpha = 1.f) {
        const auto value = std::stoul(hex.substr(1), nullptr, 16);
        return Json::array({((value >> 16) & 255) / 255.0, ((value >> 8) & 255) / 255.0,
                            (value & 255) / 255.0, static_cast<double>(alpha)});
    }
    
    /// Coordinate autore (1920x1080, top-left-down) -> coordinate wire del renderer.
    /// Origine al centro canvas, X a destra, Y verso l'ALTO (verificato sul lane
    /// pixel-truth raw: wire [-760,-340] centra un box su (200,880) px).
    /// `position` e' il centro del layer. Lo z e' assegnato da renderPlan.
    inline Json wirePos(float topDownCenterX, float topDownCenterY, float z = 0.f) {
        // Same contract as WebPageV2Pack: position is the
        // layer center in top-left-down px for X and bottom-left-up px for Y.
        return Json::array({topDownCenterX, float(kH) - topDownCenterY, z});
    }

            // recipe), while dense per-frame baked keys make the layer vanish.
            layer["animation"] = {{"tracks", tracks}};
            layer["_native_marker_core_alpha"] = std::min(1.f, alpha < 1.f ? alpha * 1.05f : 1.f);
        } else {
            geometry = {{"type", "rect"}, {"fill", rgba(hex, alpha)}};
            if (!tracks.empty()) layer["animation"] = {{"tracks", tracks}};
        }
        layer["shape"] = std::move(geometry);
        return layer;
    }
    
    inline Json ellipse(const std::string& id, float left, float top, float w, float h,
                        const std::string& hex, float alpha, int duration = 90) {
        return {{"id", id}, {"type", "shape"}, {"enable_3d", true},
                {"size", Json::array({w, h})},
                {"position", wirePos(left + w * 0.5f, top + h * 0.5f)},
                {"start_frame", 0}, {"duration_frames", duration},
                {"shape", {{"type", "ellipse"}, {"fill", rgba(hex, alpha)}}}};
    }
    
    /// Poligono arbitrario in coordinate autore (top-left-down). Il bbox diventa
    /// `size`, i punti passano relativi al centro, e `blur` aggiunge l'effetto
    /// gaussiano del decoder: e' cosi' che i Python disegnano i fogli/ritagli
    /// (`Canvas.poly`) prima del blur di placca.
    inline Json poly(const std::string& id, const std::vector<std::pair<float, float>>& pts,
                     const std::string& hex, float alpha, int duration = 90, float blur = 0.f) {
        if (pts.size() < 3) throw std::invalid_argument("poly needs at least 3 points");
        float minx = pts[0].first, maxx = minx, miny = pts[0].second, maxy = miny;
        for (const auto& p : pts) {
            minx = std::min(minx, p.first);  maxx = std::max(maxx, p.first);
            miny = std::min(miny, p.second); maxy = std::max(maxy, p.second);
        }
        const float cx = (minx + maxx) * 0.5f, cy = (miny + maxy) * 0.5f;
        Json commands = Json::array();
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < pts.size(); ++i)
            commands.push_back(Json{{"type", i == 0 ? "move_to" : "line_to"},
                                    {"point", Json::array({pts[i].first - cx, cy - pts[i].second})}});
        commands.push_back(Json{{"type", "close"}});
        Json layer = {{"id", id}, {"type", "shape"}, {"enable_3d", true},
                      {"size", Json::array({maxx - minx, maxy - miny})},
                      {"position", wirePos(cx, cy)},
                      {"start_frame", 0}, {"duration_frames", duration},
                      {"shape", {{"type", "path"}, {"path", std::move(commands)},
                                 {"fill", rgba(hex, alpha)}}}};
        if (blur > 0.f) layer["effects"] = Json::array({Json{{"type", "gaussian_blur"}, {"radius", blur}}});
        return layer;
    }
    
    /// Segmento con estremita' piatte (`Canvas.line`): poligono di 4 punti largo
    /// `width`, cosi' i tratti di penna dei reference restano nitidi/angolati.
    inline Json line(const std::string& id, float x1, float y1, float x2, float y2,
                     float width, const std::string& hex, float alpha, int duration = 90) {
        const float dx = x2 - x1, dy = y2 - y1;
        const float len = std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
        if (len <= 0.0001f) throw std::invalid_argument("line needs two distinct points");
        const float nx = -dy / len * width * 0.5f, ny = dx / len * width * 0.5f;
        return poly(id, {{x1 + nx, y1 + ny}, {x2 + nx, y2 + ny},
                         {x2 - nx, y2 - ny}, {x1 - nx, y1 - ny}}, hex, alpha, duration, 0.f);
    }
    
    namespace modules {
    struct EvidenceTimeline {
        static Json rail(const std::string& id, float left, float top, float width, float height,
                         const std::string& color, float alpha, int duration) {
            return rect(id,left,top,width,height,color,alpha,Json::array(),duration);
        }
        static Json point(const std::string& id, float left, float top, float width, float height,
                          const std::string& color, float alpha, int duration) {
            return ellipse(id,left,top,width,height,color,alpha,duration);
        }
    };
    } // namespace modules
    
    /// Blur gaussiano di placca (Python `GaussianBlur(9)`): effetto sul layer.
    inline void addBlur(Json& layer, float radius) {
        if (radius <= 0.f) return;
        Json effects = layer.contains("effects") ? layer["effects"] : Json::array();
        effects.push_back(Json{{"type", "gaussian_blur"}, {"radius", radius}});
        layer["effects"] = std::move(effects);
    }

    // Emit the five native paper-reference plans as RenderPlan V3 documents.
    #include "chronontemplate/web/WebPaperReferencePack.hpp"
    
    #include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
    
    #include <filesystem>
    #include <fstream>
    #include <iostream>
    #include <stdexcept>
    #include <string>
    
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    
    int main(int argc, char** argv) try {
        if (argc != 2) {
            throw std::runtime_error(
                "usage: chronontemplate_emit_web_paper_reference <output-dir>");
        }
        const fs::path out = fs::absolute(argv[1]);
        fs::create_directories(out);
        for (const auto recipe : chronontemplate::web::allPaperReferenceRecipes()) {
            chronontemplate::web::PaperReferenceSpec spec;
            spec.recipe = recipe;
            const auto plan = chronontemplate::web::buildPaperReferencePlan(spec);
            const fs::path path = out / (spec.planName() + ".plan.json");
            std::ofstream file(path);
            if (!file) throw std::runtime_error("cannot write " + path.string());
            file << plan.dump(2) << '\n';
            std::cout << path.string() << '\n';
        }
        return 0;
    } catch (const std::exception& error) {
        std::cerr << error.what() << '\n';
        return 1;
    }
    /// (center_px = (960 + pos.x, 540 - pos.y)) e `size` e' la cornice in px, con
    /// `fit: cover` che ritaglia al suo interno. Misure: size 1440x257 a [0,0] ->
    /// bbox x 240..1680 y 411..668; a [232,0] -> x 472..1912 (solo +232 in x);
    /// size 1920x1080 a [0,0] -> cornice piena.
    inline Json wireImagePos(float left, float top, float w, float h, float z = 0.f) {
        return Json::array({left + w * 0.5f - float(kW) * 0.5f,
                            float(kH) * 0.5f - (top + h * 0.5f), z});
    }

                      float w, float h, int duration = 90) {
        return {{"id", id}, {"type", "image"}, {"enable_3d", true}, {"asset", asset},
                {"position", wireImagePos(left, top, w, h)},
                {"size", Json::array({w, h})}, {"fit", "cover"},
                {"start_frame", 0}, {"duration_frames", duration}};
    }
    
    inline Json easedTrack(const std::string& property, float from, float to,
                           int start, int span, const std::string& easing) {
        return {{"property", property}, {"easing", easing},
                {"keyframes", Json::array({
                    Json{{"frame", 0}, {"value", from}},
                    Json{{"frame", std::max(1, start)}, {"value", from}},
                    Json{{"frame", start + span}, {"value", to}}})}};
    }
    
    template <typename Push>
    Json sortedKeys(Push push) {
        Json keys = Json::array();
        push(keys);
        std::sort(keys.begin(), keys.end(), [](const Json& a, const Json& b) {
            return a["frame"].get<int>() < b["frame"].get<int>();
        });
        return keys;
    }
    
    /// Marker/highlighter: opacity + scale_x crescono mentre il centro scorre,
    /// cosi il blocco si svela da sinistra come nei Python.
    inline Json legacySweepTracks(float width, int begin, int span) {
        auto reveal = [&](Json& keys) {
            keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", std::max(0, begin - 8)}, {"value", 0.0}});
            keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", begin}, {"value", 0.0}});
            keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", begin + span}, {"value", 1.0}});
        };
        auto slide = [&](Json& keys) {
            keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", begin}, {"value", -width * 0.5}});
            keys.push_back(Json{{"frame", begin + span}, {"value", 0.0}});
        };
        return Json::array({
            Json{{"property", "opacity"}, {"easing", "in_out_cubic"}, {"keyframes", sortedKeys(reveal)}},
            Json{{"property", "scale_x"}, {"easing", "in_out_cubic"}, {"keyframes", sortedKeys(reveal)}},
            Json{{"property", "position_x"}, {"easing", "in_out_cubic"}, {"keyframes", sortedKeys(slide)}}});
    }

    /// renderer conserva l'ordine autoriale del builder.
    inline Json renderPlan(const std::string& jobId, int duration, const Json& layers,
                           const Json& cameraSamplesJson) {
        // The current RenderPlan contract applies the plan camera directly. The
        // old writer baked a Python crop affine into layer tracks as well, which
        // double-transformed every shot after the camera pass changed. Keep one
        // transform authority: the camera stays static and the layers keep only
        // their authored tracks (marker sweeps, pops, etc.).
        (void)cameraSamplesJson;

        for (const Json& authored : layers) {
            Json layer = authored;
            const bool hasMarkerCore = layer.contains("_native_marker_core_alpha");
            const double coreAlpha = hasMarkerCore ? layer["_native_marker_core_alpha"].get<double>() : 1.0;
            layer.erase("_native_marker_core_alpha");
            layer.erase("_v4_highlight");
            // Painter order: i layer successivi siedono piu' vicini alla camera
            // (camera a z=-1158: z piu' negativo = piu' vicino). Il core del
            // marker segue subito il bordo grezzo cosi' resta sopra di esso e
            // sotto i glifi del testo.
            auto pushWithDepth = [&](Json l) {
                if (l.contains("position") && l["position"].is_array() &&
                    l["position"].size() >= 3)
                    l["position"][2] = -kLayerDepthStep * float(stack.size());
                stack.push_back(std::move(l));

                core.erase("_v4_highlight");

                const float w = authored["size"][0].get<float>();
                const float h = authored["size"][1].get<float>();
                core["id"] = id + "_core";
                core["size"] = Json::array({w, h * 0.56f});
                core["shape"] = {{"type", "rect"}, {"fill", authored["shape"]["fill"]}};
                if (core["shape"]["fill"].is_array()) core["shape"]["fill"][3] = coreAlpha;
                pushWithDepth(std::move(core));

                {"canvas", {{"width", kW}, {"height", kH}, {"fps_num", kFps}, {"fps_den", 1},
                            {"duration_frames", duration}}},
                {"layers", std::move(stack)}, {"camera", staticCamera()}};

    #include "chronontemplate/web/WebShotJson.hpp"
    #include "chronontemplate/web/WebPaperReferencePack.hpp"
    
    #include <filesystem>
    #include <fstream>
    #include <iostream>
    #include <stdexcept>
    
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    using chronontemplate::web::shot::Json;
    using namespace chronontemplate::web::shot;
    
    namespace {
    void writePlan(const fs::path& out, const std::string& name, const Json& plan) {
        std::ofstream file(out / (name + ".plan.json"));
        if (!file) throw std::runtime_error("cannot write plan: " + name);
        file << plan.dump(2) << '\n';
    }
    
    Json pillPressPlan() {
        constexpr int d = 180;
        constexpr float x = 315.f;
        constexpr float body = 32.f;
        Json layers = Json::array();
        auto bg = rect("paper", 0, 0, 1920, 1080, "#F4F2EA", 1.f, Json::array(), d);
        addNoiseVignette(bg, 0.018f, 45119, 0.42f);
        layers.push_back(bg);
    
        const char* title = "Drug traffickers use pill presses to press fentanyl into pills";
        const float titleSize = 48.f;
        layers.push_back(textLayer("title", title, 315.f, 254.f, titleSize, kSerifBold,
                                   "#171614", d));
    
        const char* line1 = "oxycodone, Xanax, and Adderall — drugs that look identical to";
        const char* line2 = "the real thing. But when those pills actually contain fentanyl,";
        const char* line3 = "methamphetamine, and other deadly drugs, a single dose can kill.";
        const float y1 = 394.f, y2 = 454.f, y3 = 514.f;
        const float greenW = measuredTextWidth(title, body, kSerif) + 14.f;
        const float greenY = 339.f;
        auto green = rect("highlight_green", x - 4.f, greenY, greenW, 39.f,
                          "#C9DC28", 0.92f, sweepTracks(greenW, 22, 24), d);
        layers.push_back(green);
    
        const float prefix = measuredTextWidth("the real thing. But ", body, kSerif);
        const float yellowW = measuredTextWidth("when those pills actually contain fentanyl,", body, kSerif) + 10.f;
        auto yellow = rect("highlight_yellow", x + prefix - 4.f, y2 - 5.f, yellowW, 39.f,
                           "#F2C500", 0.96f, sweepTracks(yellowW, 54, 26), d);
        layers.push_back(yellow);
        const float yellow2W = measuredTextWidth("methamphetamine, and other deadly drugs,", body, kSerif) + 10.f;
        layers.push_back(rect("highlight_yellow_2", x - 4.f, y3 - 5.f, yellow2W, 39.f,
                              "#F2C500", 0.96f, sweepTracks(yellow2W, 78, 25), d));
    
        layers.push_back(textLayer("paragraph_1", line1, x, y1, body, kSerif, "#171614", d));
        layers.push_back(textLayer("paragraph_2", line2, x, y2, body, kSerif, "#171614", d));
        layers.push_back(textLayer("paragraph_3", line3, x, y3, body, kSerif, "#171614", d));
        Json plan = renderPlan("pill_press_reference_cpp_v2", d, layers, cameraSamples(d));
        plan["camera"]["dof"] = {{"enabled", true}, {"focus_distance", 1158.06f},
                                  {"max_blur", 2.5f}, {"highlight_gain", 0.15f}};
        plan["camera"]["f_stop"] = 5.6f;
        plan["output"] = {{"path", "pill_press_reference_cpp_v2.mp4"}, {"format", "mp4"}, {"codec", "h264"}};
        return plan;
    }
    
    Json archivePlan() {
        chronontemplate::web::PaperReferenceSpec spec;
        spec.recipe = chronontemplate::web::PaperReferenceRecipe::NewspaperTilt;
        spec.durationFrames = 180;
        Json plan = chronontemplate::web::buildPaperReferencePlan(spec);
        plan["job_id"] = "archive_page_2_5d_dof_cpp_v1";
        plan["camera"]["dof"] = {{"enabled", true}, {"focus_distance", 1158.06f},
                                  {"max_blur", 2.5f}, {"highlight_gain", 0.2f}};
        plan["camera"]["f_stop"] = 2.5f;
        plan["output"] = {{"path", "archive_page_2_5d_dof_cpp_v1.mp4"}, {"format", "mp4"}, {"codec", "h264"}};
        return plan;
    }
    }
    
    int main(int argc, char** argv) try {
        if (argc != 2) throw std::runtime_error("usage: chronontemplate_emit_user_reference_recreations <output-dir>");
        const fs::path out = fs::absolute(argv[1]);
        fs::create_directories(out);
        writePlan(out, "pill_press_reference_cpp_v2", pillPressPlan());
        writePlan(out, "archive_page_2_5d_dof_cpp_v1", archivePlan());
        std::cout << out.string() << '\n';
        return 0;
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        std::cerr << e.what() << '\n';
        return 1;
    }

        const float topEff = vMiddle ? top - h * 0.5f : top;
        Json position = wirePos(leftEff + w * 0.5f, topEff + h * 0.5f);
        Json layer = {{"id", id}, {"type", "text"}, {"text", text},
                      {"size", Json::array({w, h})},
                      {"position", std::move(position)},
                      {"enable_3d", true},
                      {"style", {{"font", font}, {"font_size", size}, {"fill", fill}}},
                      {"start_frame", 0}, {"duration_frames", duration}};
        if (opacity != 1.f) layer["opacity"] = opacity;
        Json animators = Json::array();
        if (blur > 0.f) animators.push_back(modules::FocusMask::textBlur(id, blur, duration));
        if (tracking != 0.f) animators.push_back(trackingAnimator(id, tracking, duration));
        if (!animators.empty()) layer["text_animators"] = std::move(animators);
        // `slot` is kept in the helper signature for source compatibility, but
        // static text stays at its authored position. The old generic fade/rise
        // track wrote absolute position_y values and pushed unrelated headlines
        // off canvas. Python shots animate the camera/marker per shot instead.
        (void)slot;
        return layer;
    }

    };

## Assistant

L’anteprima archivistica esistente usava per errore un asset di giornale sui Giants, quindi non la considero valida e non la userò come secondo video. La sto sostituendo con il documento Mailchimp delle immagini Drive, ricreato in C++ con camera inclinata e DOF f/2.5; dopo mostro il frame corretto per approvazione.

## Assistant

Ho aggiornato sul Drive il primo video: [Pill Press Threat — Full HD](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1H9FA3rBXQY3Yz7wEs6ZDMGka0ySjVDx7/view?usp=drivesdk). È a 1920×1080, 30 fps, 6 secondi, renderizzato con Vulkan e NVENC; ho ricentrato il testo e allineato gli evidenziatori alle righe.

Ho authorato in C++ anche la ricostruzione del documento Mailchimp con prospettiva 2.5D e DOF f/2.5. [Apri il frame di anteprima](</tmp/chronontemplate_cpp_recreations/archive_preview_final.png>). Il codice è in [emit_user_reference_recreations.cpp](/home/pierone/src/go-master/projects/Pyt/VeloxEditing/ChrononTemplate/tools/web_presets/emit_user_reference_recreations.cpp); il target C++ compila.

Per questo secondo soggetto ho renderizzato solo l’anteprima: le istruzioni visuali del progetto richiedono la tua approvazione del frame prima del video completo. Le immagini bastano per ricreare lo stile; senza il video sorgente non posso copiare esattamente il movimento o sincronizzare l’audio.

## User

Perfetto, ora ho accesso ai due repository GitHub. Il contesto è completamente diverso da After Effects: puoi ricreare questi effetti direttamente nel tuo ecosistema C++ con ChrononTemplate + ChrononMotion + Chronon3D.

Dai README emerge questa separazione architetturale:
Modulo	Responsabilità
ChrononTemplate	Composizione, layout e preset
ChrononMotion	Camera, trasformazioni e animazioni
Chronon3D	Rendering, materiali, testo, DOF e compositing
RenderingGen	Intento editoriale e contenuti

Ho già individuato in ChrononTemplate una famiglia particolarmente pertinente: DocumentaryReferenceStills, che include anche un estratto testuale evidenziato e un effetto CRT.

Non partirei quindi da zero: cercherei di riutilizzare le primitive esistenti e costruire due preset documentali parametrizzabili.
1. Le funzionalità che hai già implementato
Ho trovato componenti ancora più interessanti nel codice sorgente.
Componente esistente	Utilizzo per i tuoi overlay
ModernDocumentaryPack	Highlighter, rack focus, effetti analogici
DocumentaryReferenceStills	Carta, rumore, estratti documentali
HighlightingV2	Evidenziatori irregolari e animati
CameraMotionPack	Movimento prospettico della camera
WebPageHighlightPack	Evidenziazione animata di articoli
ArchivalLensLook	Trattamento ottico da archivio

In particolare, ModernDocumentaryRecipe::VoxHighlight è già concettualmente molto vicino al secondo screenshot.

Fonti: ModernDocumentaryPack.hpp · HighlightingV2.hpp · DocumentaryReferenceStills.cpp
2. Primo overlay — Cinematic Document Macro
Mockup schematico del trattamento prospettico e della messa a fuoco.
Questo non è semplicemente un documento ruotato. La prospettiva comprime progressivamente il testo verso destra, mentre la parte più vicina all'osservatore appare più grande.
Impostazioni di partenza
Parametro	Valore consigliato
Risoluzione	1920 × 1080
Durata	5–6 secondi
Camera FOV verticale	30–40°
Inclinazione Y	25–35°
Inclinazione X	8–15°
Roll apparente	8–12°
Dolly push-in	5–10%
Rumore carta	0.012–0.025
Vignette amount	0.65–0.80
Vignette radius	0.55–0.65
Vignette softness	0.60–0.80
Aberrazione cromatica	0.5–1.5 px

Sono valori proposti per riprodurre il reference, non valori estratti dal video originale.
Struttura della scena
Camera 3D reale, documento su un piano fisso, fuoco sulla porzione di testo rilevante.
Userei un'unica superficie documentale, con carta e testo complanari. La camera deve muoversi, non il documento. Questo permette di ottenere prospettiva e DOF coerenti senza simulare manualmente la sfocatura di ogni riga.

Chronon3D dichiara esplicitamente il supporto a proiezione, depth of field, motion blur e compositing. ChrononMotion gestisce invece l'authoring cinematografico della camera.

Fonte: Chronon3D README.
3. Secondo overlay — Document Marker Highlight
Mockup del documento frontale con marker colorati e trattamento ottico.
Per questo overlay hai già implementato quasi tutto il necessario. Nel sorgente di ModernDocumentaryPack.cpp esiste persino la funzione sweepTracks(), che accoppia scale_x e position_x affinché il marker cresca verso destra mantenendo fisso il bordo sinistro.

È esattamente il comportamento che serve.
Evidenziatore realistico
Marker reveal
100%




[x] Bordi irregolari
Simulazione interattiva del marker, non un render del motore Chronon3D.
Non utilizzerei soltanto un rettangolo con opacità animata. Il reference presenta piccole imperfezioni ai bordi tipiche di un evidenziatore fisico.

Riutilizzerei:
- highlightStroke() di HighlightingV2.
- HighlightStyle::rough.
- sweepTracks() per il reveal orizzontale.
- Blend mode multiply.
- Effetto roughen_edges per rendere meno geometrico il contorno.
- Misurazione del testo tramite la pipeline tipografica esistente.
Parametri suggeriti
Proprietà	Valore
Paper color	#E6E3E1
Text color	#353535
Marker green	#69BC43
Marker yellow	#E7C132
Marker opacity	0.75–0.90
Marker roughness	1–3 px
Body font	Inter Regular, 29–32 px
Title font	Inter Bold, 38–42 px
Scanline spacing	2–3 px
Scanline amount	0.015–0.035
Reveal duration	18–30 frame per riga

Quando il testo va a capo, il marker deve essere suddiviso in due segmenti e non in un unico rettangolo.
4. Il trattamento ottico comune
Questo è probabilmente l'aspetto più importante dei due reference. Entrambi hanno una forte caduta di luminosità ai bordi, accompagnata da una leggera morbidezza dell'immagine.

Hai già gli effetti necessari in Chronon3D.

Partirei da questo blocco, utilizzando i nomi dei parametri effettivamente presenti in ModernDocumentaryPack.cpp:
[
  {
    "type": "noise",
    "amount": 0.018,
    "seed": 731,
    "size": 1.0,
    "animated": false
  },
  {
    "type": "chromatic_aberration",
    "red_offset": 0.8,

  },

    "type": "scanlines",
    "spacing_px": 2.5,

  },

  }

Applicherei questi effetti alla composizione documentale risolta, evitando che ogni singola riga di testo abbia la propria vignettatura.

Per il primo overlay ridurrei o disabiliterei le scanline, privilegiando la texture della carta e il DOF.

Fonte: ModernDocumentaryPack.cpp.
5. Come strutturerei il nuovo pack
Non aggiungerei due ulteriori scene hardcoded a DocumentaryReferenceStills.cpp. Creerei un pack riutilizzabile, che RenderingGen possa alimentare con qualsiasi documento.
include/chronontemplate/web/
    DocumentEvidencePack.hpp

src/chronontemplate/web/
    DocumentEvidencePack.cpp

tools/web_presets/
    emit_document_evidence.cpp

tests/
    document_evidence_pack.cpp


Come API proposta:
enum class DocumentEvidenceRecipe {
    CinematicMacro,
    MarkerHighlight
};

struct DocumentHighlight {
    std::size_t byteStart;
    std::size_t byteEnd;

    std::string color{"#E7C132"};

    int startFrame{30};
    int revealFrames{24};
    float opacity{0.85f};
    bool rough{true};
};

struct DocumentEvidenceSpec {
    DocumentEvidenceRecipe recipe{
        DocumentEvidenceRecipe::CinematicMacro
    };

    std::string title;
    std::string body;
    std::string sourceImage;

    std::vector<DocumentHighlight> highlights;

    int durationFrames{180};
    int fps{30};

    float vignette{0.78f};
    float grain{0.018f};
    float cameraPush{0.08f};

    bool depthOfField{true};
    bool scanlines{false};
};


Questa è una proposta di nuova API, non una classe già presente nel repository.

7. Cosa manca realmente a Chronon
Funzionalità	Stato dall'analisi
Camera prospettica 3D	Presente
Depth of field	Presente
Marker animato	Presente
Multiply blending	Presente
Roughen edges	Presente
Vignettatura	Presente
Aberrazione cromatica	Presente
Scanline	Presente
Preset identico al reference	Da realizzare e verificare
Highlight automatico multilinea	Da verificare e integrare

Non vedo la necessità, allo stato attuale, di modificare il core di Chronon3D. Hai già le primitive principali per realizzare entrambi gli effetti.

Realizzerei una famiglia DocumentEvidencePack con due recipe iniziali:
- document_evidence_cinematic_macro_v1
- document_evidence_marker_highlight_v1
Successivamente la renderei compatibile sia con documenti PNG acquisiti da PDF reali, sia con documenti ricostruiti tramite layer testuali nativi.

La parte da curare maggiormente non è l'animazione, ma il realismo ottico: prospettiva, messa a fuoco selettiva, imperfezioni del marker e vignettatura.

Ho consultato i sorgenti dei repository, ma non ho compilato il progetto, effettuato rendering di prova o modificato file su GitHub. I parametri e i mockup proposti sono quindi una base progettuale da validare visivamente, non risultati certificati del motore. fa cager quello che hai fatto prima erea molto più simile

    Json rgba(const std::string& hex, float alpha = 1.f) {
        if (hex.size() != 7 || hex.front() != '#')
            throw std::invalid_argument("ModernDocumentaryPack: color must be #RRGGBB");
        const unsigned value = static_cast<unsigned>(std::stoul(hex.substr(1), nullptr, 16));
        return Json::array({((value >> 16) & 255U) / 255.0, ((value >> 8) & 255U) / 255.0,
                            (value & 255U) / 255.0, static_cast<double>(alpha)});
    }
    
    float wireY(float topDownY) { return static_cast<float>(kH) - topDownY; }
    
    Json key(int frame, double value) {
        return Json{{"frame", frame}, {"value", value}};
    }
    
    Json track(const std::string& property, Json keys, const std::string& easing = "linear") {
        return Json{{"property", property}, {"easing", easing}, {"keyframes", std::move(keys)}};
    }
    
    /// Left-to-right marker reveal. scale_x and position_x are coupled so the
    /// authored left edge stays pinned while the right edge travels.
    Json sweepTracks(float width, int begin, int span) {
        Json scaleKeys = Json::array();
        Json positionKeys = Json::array();
        scaleKeys.push_back(key(0, 0.0));
        scaleKeys.push_back(key(begin, 0.0));
        scaleKeys.push_back(key(begin + span, 1.0));
        scaleKeys.push_back(key(begin + span + 1, 1.0));
        positionKeys.push_back(key(0, -width * 0.5));
        positionKeys.push_back(key(begin, -width * 0.5));
        positionKeys.push_back(key(begin + span, 0.0));
        positionKeys.push_back(key(begin + span + 1, 0.0));
        return Json::array({
            track("opacity", Json::array({key(0, 0.0), key(begin, 0.0),
                                          key(begin + 1, 1.0), key(begin + span + 1, 1.0)})),
            track("scale_x", std::move(scaleKeys), "in_out_cubic"),
            track("position_x", std::move(positionKeys), "in_out_cubic")});
    }
    
    Json effectNoise(float amount, unsigned seed, float size = 1.f, bool animated = true) {
        return Json{{"type", "noise"}, {"amount", amount}, {"seed", seed}, {"size", size},
                    {"animated", animated}};
    }
    
    Json effectVignette(float amount, float radius = 0.72f, float softness = 0.58f) {
        return Json{{"type", "vignette"}, {"amount", amount}, {"radius", radius},
                    {"softness", softness}};
    }
    
    Json effectGlow(float radius, float intensity, const std::string& color) {
        return Json{{"type", "glow"}, {"radius", radius}, {"intensity", intensity},
                    {"color", rgba(color, 1.f)}};
    }
    
    Json effectBloom(float threshold, float radius, float intensity) {
        return Json{{"type", "bloom"}, {"threshold", threshold}, {"radius", radius},
                    {"intensity", intensity}};
    }
    
    Json effectScanlines(float spacing, float amount, float phase = 0.f) {
        return Json{{"type", "scanlines"}, {"spacing_px", spacing}, {"amount", amount},
                    {"phase", phase}};
    }
    
    Json effectChromatic(float red, float blue) {
        return Json{{"type", "chromatic_aberration"}, {"red_offset", red},
                    {"blue_offset", blue}};
    }
    
    Json effectMeshGlitch(int cols = 8, int rows = 8, float amount = 0.012f) {
        // The decoder expects cols*rows x/y pairs, not one scalar per grid point.
        Json offsets = Json::array();
        for (int row = 0; row < rows; ++row) {
            const float sign = (row % 2 == 0) ? 1.f : -1.f;
            for (int col = 0; col < cols; ++col) {
                offsets.push_back(sign * amount * (1.f + static_cast<float>(col % 3) * 0.2f));
                offsets.push_back(0.f);
            }
        }
        return Json{{"type", "mesh_warp"}, {"cols", cols}, {"rows", rows},
                    {"smoothness", 0.f}, {"offsets", std::move(offsets)}};
    }
    
    Json effectLens(float curvature, float scale = 1.08f) {
        return Json{{"type", "lens_distortion"}, {"curvature", curvature},
                    {"scale", scale}, {"center", Json::array({0.5, 0.5})}};
    }
    
    Json effectDirectional(float angle, float length, int samples) {
        return Json{{"type", "directional_blur"}, {"angle", angle}, {"length", length},
                    {"samples", samples}};
    }
    
    Json shape(const std::string& id, const std::string& type, float left, float top,
               float width, float height, const std::string& color, float alpha,
               float z, Json animation = Json::array(), const std::string& blend = "normal") {
        // Shape layers are center-relative, unlike text layers: the renderer maps
        // screen_x = 960 + position.x and screen_y = 540 - position.y.
        Json layer = {{"id", id}, {"type", "shape"}, {"enable_3d", true},
                      {"position", Json::array({left + width * 0.5f - 960.f,
                                                540.f - (top + height * 0.5f), z})},
                      {"size", Json::array({width, height})},
                      {"start_frame", 0},
                      {"shape", {{"type", type}, {"fill", rgba(color, alpha)}}}};
        if (!animation.empty()) layer["animation"] = Json{{"tracks", std::move(animation)}};
        if (blend != "normal") layer["blend_mode"] = blend;
        return layer;
    }
    
    Json rect(const std::string& id, float left, float top, float width, float height,
              const std::string& color, float alpha, float z, Json animation = Json::array(),
              const std::string& blend = "normal") {
        return shape(id, "rect", left, top, width, height, color, alpha, z,
                                 {"fps_den", 1}, {"duration_frames", duration}}},
                     {"camera", std::move(camera)},
                     {"camera_samples", std::move(cameraSamples)},
                     {"layers", std::move(layers)},
                     {"output", {{"path", jobId + ".mp4"}, {"format", "mp4"},
                                 {"codec", "h264"}}},
                     {"lighting_rig", {{"key_direction", Json::array({0.f, 0.f, 1.f})},
                                       {"key_intensity", 0.f},
                                       {"key_color", Json::array({1.f, 1.f, 1.f, 1.f})},
                                       {"ambient_intensity", 1.f},
                                       {"ambient_color", Json::array({1.f, 1.f, 1.f, 1.f})},
                                       {"rim_enabled", false}}}};
        if (!temporalBlur.is_null()) plan["temporal_motion_blur"] = std::move(temporalBlur);
        return plan;
    }

    Json buildSplitGlitch(int duration) {
    // ChrononTemplate — Modern Documentary pack.
    //
    // Five native RenderPlan V3 looks distilled from the supplied modern
    // documentary references:
    //
    //   VoxHighlight   paper article, left-anchored multiply highlighter, subject
    //                  cutout, rack focus and floating dust.
    //   SplitGlitch    torn split composition, glowing energy divider, UI card in
    //                  Z-space with chromatic/mesh/slice glitch treatment.
    //   MacroUiRain    macro comment UI, typewriter sentence, layered crowd
    //                  silhouettes and a banknote particle rain with HUD.
    //   KineticType    four 3D typographic beats, left-to-right bars and a
    //                  whip-pan camera with a 180-degree temporal shutter.
    //   VhsCarousel    CRT frame, spring-overshoot logo carousel, hot title and
    //                  analog scanline/chroma wear.
    //
    // Every look is authored as ordinary `chronon.render-plan.v3` data. Chronon3D
    // owns rasterization, effects, camera sampling and encoding; this module owns
    // the design vocabulary and timing. No browser, DOM or live JS is involved.
    //
    // The pack deliberately uses the renderer's existing primitives:
    //   * multiply blend + shape scale/position tracks (highlighter),
    //   * camera_samples with thin-lens DoF (rack focus),
    //   * text_animators + a character selector (typewriter),
    //   * temporal_motion_blur + per-frame camera_samples (whip pan),
    //   * chromatic_aberration, mesh_warp, scanlines, retro_tv, roughen_edges,
    //     lens_distortion, glow/bloom and directional_blur (analog/UI wear),
    //   * particle_emitter sprite, rotation and angular_velocity fields.
    //
    // The banknote rain is a 2.5D environment emitter: it uses the existing
    // per-particle sprite rotation and fake depth/DoF fields. It is not a claim of
    // a full six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body particle solver.
    #ifndef CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_MODERN_DOCUMENTARY_PACK_HPP
    #define CHRONONTEMPLATE_WEB_MODERN_DOCUMENTARY_PACK_HPP
    
    #include <array>
    #include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
    #include <string>
    
    namespace chronontemplate::web {
    
    enum class ModernDocumentaryRecipe : unsigned char {
        VoxHighlight,
        SplitGlitch,
        MacroUiRain,
        KineticType,
        VhsCarousel
    };

        [[nodiscard]] std::string planName() const;
        [[nodiscard]] std::string outputStem() const;
    };
    
    /// Complete `chronon.render-plan.v3` document for one look.
